articleTitle: Measurement of power quality factors in electrical networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Summary form only given. A microprocessor based system that correctly estimates asymmetry and harmonics rating is presented. The measurement method, the measuring channel structure, the DSP algorithm and software structure are described.

articleTitle: The Australian voltage standard using a 1 V Josephson array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Summary form only given. The Australian voltage standard uses a 1 V Josephson junction array fabricated by NIST and excited at 73 GHz. The entire system is described, including: the liquid-helium dewar designed to permit permanent immersion of the array, the array bias circuitry, the Gunn-diode driver circuitry, the system of low-thermal key-switches, and other techniques of minimising small errors and interference. The effect of various guard and ground connections to secondary electronic standards is described. A complete Type A and Type B uncertainty analysis of the system is given.

articleTitle: Linear microparticle trap operating in air
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents a linear a.c. trap operating in air. Microparticle trapping phenomenon has been achieved. Various spatial patterns made of a few up to thousands of microparticles stable for a very long time have been observed. The microparticle charge and specific charge have been independently determined.

articleTitle: Procedure to calibrate a network-analyzer for the measurement of voltages at any impedance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A calibration procedure for network analyzes was developed, which makes you able to measure the absolute value of the voltage a the current at the calibration plane or the power propagating towards the device under test. These measurements are independent of the impedance at the calibration plane.

articleTitle: Preliminary results on the analog-to-digital converter based on RSFQ logic
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The first laboratory prototype of a superconductor analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with on-chip fast digital signal processing has been designed and tested at internal clock frequencies up to 7 GHz. Estimated accuracy of the prototype is about 12 bit for 7 MHz signal bandwidth; at lower frequencies the dynamic range increases at least as fast as the reciprocal bandwidth. The single-chip (5/spl times/5 mm/sup 2/) device contains 1778 Josephson junctions and dissipates power at about 0.5 mW.

articleTitle: Loading errors in low voltage AC measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The new generation of AC instruments has increased the demand on accuracy. To minimize errors due to loading the input impedances of three AC instruments used at SP has been measured. In two of the instruments a variation in the input impedance due to sampling was observed.

articleTitle: Highly sensitive picoampere meter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have developed a sensitive picoampere meter for accurate room temperature measurement of currents below 10 pA. The main characteristics of the instrument are an extremely low input current, far below 1 fA, and fully automated operation. Preliminary calibration of the instrument with a separately developed facility has been done at the accuracy level of a few parts in 10/sup 4/.

articleTitle: Millimeter apparatus for transmission line and dielectric material measurements by multifrequency methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: It is important to measure not only total reflection coefficient (RC) but the distribution of discontinuities in transmission lines. Frequency dispersion makes it difficult to apply direct time-reflectometry in millimeter waveband waveguides. That is why it is more preferable to measure RC at a set of frequencies and transform experimental data from frequency to time domain using one of the spectral numerical algorithms. Equidistant wave-number sampling allows one to overcome frequency dispersion. Simplicity of a scalar reflectometer (SR) application is very attractive. Such modification of SR as comparison reflectometer measuring the sum of reference reflection and reflection of the device under test (DUT) can be used to obtain the distribution of discontinuities as a result of the transformation into time domain. The sum of exponentials is the general model for not only the distribution of discontinuities in waveguides but also the distribution of interfaces of layers in dielectric materials. Peculiarity of the latter task is positioning materials not in a waveguide but in free space. The authors describe the principles of an original six-port method and the scalar reflectometry, and present some experimental results.

articleTitle: Absolute determination of loss angle
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A guard ring capacitor has been constructed and is used for absolute determinations of the loss angle of capacitors at SP (Swedish National Testing and Research Institute). The accuracy is estimated to /spl plusmn/1 ppm (k=2). The main source of error is from the quadrature errors in the capacitance bridge.

articleTitle: A new self-calibrating instrument for voltage transformer calibration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new current comparator and digital ratio-meter based self-calibrating instrument for voltage transformer calibration has been developed at the Technical University of Budapest. The instrument measures the in-phase and quadrature components of the complex error by means of a digital ratio-meter. The built-in programmable analog signal processor facilitates comparison and direct calibration of voltage transformers of different ratios. Advanced hardware and software technology ensure complete on-site self-calibration of the instrument. The basic accuracy of the instrument is /spl plusmn/2 ppm with 1 ppm resolution.

articleTitle: Micropotentiometers as ac-dc transfer standards for low-voltage measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Micropotentiometers with commercial single-junction thermal converters and laboratory-made disk resistors are used at PTB as ac-dc voltage transfer standards at low voltages from 1 mV to 100 mV and frequencies from 10 Hz to 1 MHz. The measurement results and the estimated uncertainties are compared with those of other institutes at the international level.

articleTitle: Sensor for high-air-humidity measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The humidity sensor using the sensitive capacitive-dependent crystal is described. Presented is the probe sensitivity (dependence of df on the dCx). In addition the new idea of excitation of the entire humidity sensor with stochastic test signals is described, and the humidity surface-measuring method is given. It includes the influence of test signals of the weighting function uncertainty and of the A/D-D/A conversion. The results of humidity measurement with the excitation signals are shown experimentally. The uncertainty of the surface humidity measurement is less than 0.2% (T=15 to 25/spl deg/C and humidity=50 to 98%).

articleTitle: Measurements of the dielectric relaxation spectra of nine liquids and binary mixtures at 20/spl deg/C and microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: New measurements of the dielectric permittivity of nine liquids and binary mixtures have been made in the range 1 to 12 GHz. The measurements are combined with data from the literature and Debye type relaxation equations are fitted. Conclusions are formed about the number of relaxation processes for each liquid.

articleTitle: Full characterization of microwave low noise HEMTs: measurements vs. modeling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The up to date version working up to 40 GHz of a noise figure measuring system for the characterization of transistors in terms of noise, gain and scattering parameters through noise figure measurements only is presented. In the fully automated version the method is rapid and very accurate but it is so difficult to assemble and handle that a very skilled operator is needed. This can be accepted in a research laboratory but is a very hard task for manufacturers to test their products. So, we have recently set-up a "simplified" method which is easier to run and accurate enough for industrial applications. The method is based on the extraction of a noise model of the transistor from measurements of [S] through an automatic network analyzer and of one noise figure only.

articleTitle: Absolute calibration of a 100 KV DC divider
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An absolute determination of the ratio of a 100 kV DC divider has been made. A new Zener device that has recently become available has been used in a step-up mode to obtain the divider ratio. The uncertainty of the determination is 5.5 ppm.

articleTitle: Development of new microcalorimeters in the frequency range 40-75 GHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This article describes the set up of a measurement bench available above 40 GHz for power calibrations. It allows one to determine the efficiency of millimeter-wave power detectors. This equipment achieves the junction between 40 GHz (R 320 waveguide) and 75 GHz (R 900 waveguide) in this domain.

articleTitle: Calibration of the standard resistors by means of the standard capacitors and precise digital voltmeters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The calibration is carried out by measuring the ratios of voltages on an auxiliary resistor, once as a result of the current flowing through the previously calibrated capacitance standard, and the other time as a result of the current through the resistance standard. Using these voltage ratios, obtained with DC and low frequency AC current, measured by the precise digital voltmeters, a resistance standard can be calibrated with the uncertainty of 0.2 ppm.

articleTitle: Iterative structure of Winograd FFT algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A 1D-to-1D mapping is designed to get an iterative structure of the Winograd FFT algorithm (WFTA). With this new representation, the WFTA features a unified computational structure which is the same as that of the Cooley-Tukey algorithm.

articleTitle: A new method for the measurement of very low speeds using a multiple-electrode capacitive sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A novel method for the measurement of low speed by using a low-cost capacitive sensor is presented. Its main advantages are its simplicity, low cost and the very low speed that can be measured with a relatively high resolution in a short measurement time.

articleTitle: A broadband free-space dielectric properties measurement system at millimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A free-space measurement system operating in the 75-95 GHz range is used to measure the complex transmission coefficient of a vertical polarized wave through a planar sample for different incidence angles. The complex permittivity is obtained form the measurement data by means of a nonlinear least-squares estimate. The multiple reflections between the transmitting and receiving horn antenna are removed by the time domain gating technique. A dielectric lens collimates the beam of the transmitting horn antenna for minimisation of diffraction effects at the edges of the sample. The performance of the measurement setup has been tested using glass samples. An accuracy of better than 0.04% and 0.5% for the real part and imaginary part of the complex permittivity, respectively, has been achieved.

articleTitle: Wide-band inductive voltage divider for ac voltage calibrations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes an inductive voltage divider developed for fitting the low-voltage range measuring instruments to the ac-dc transfer standards for voltages of 1 V. The divider, the associated circuit and the calibration procedure allow one to compare the standard and unknown ac instrument at 1:10 ratio in the frequency band from 1 kHz to 1 MHz. The construction and uncertainty budget are given.

articleTitle: A new capacitive precision liquid-level sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The liquid-level sensor consists of a low-cost planar electrode structure, a capacitance-controlled oscillator and a microcontroller. The sensor is able to measure absolute levels of conducting and non-conducting liquids with a 1 mm accuracy over a 4 m range. The system has a high resolution of 0.1 mm at short measuring times of only 0.2 s. Slow level movements of 0.02 mm/h can be detected within 18 min.

articleTitle: The basis of Croatian electromagnetic metrology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Measuring equipment, standards, methods and procedures necessary to ensure the traceability in the laboratory calibration system of electromagnetic quantities, are described. The accuracy scale and appropriate uncertainties appearing at the specific levels when measuring electric quantities such as voltage, current, power, resistance, capacitance etc., are analyzed. The research directions and possibilities of the international and national interlaboratory connections, are discussed.

articleTitle: Automatic testing system for calibration of ac/dc transfer standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In this paper, an automatic testing system developed for the calibration of the ac/dc transfer standards is presented. An accurate uncertainty analysis model for this system is fully discussed. Besides, the system is assessed in relation to its accuracy, efficiency and its capability to carry out full range calibration in a much less time period than that of manual operation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the AC quantized Hall resistance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The AC quantized Hall resistance (QHR) has been evaluated with respect to its dependence on sample, sample temperature, plateau flatness, longitudinal resistance, and step value.

articleTitle: Conversion of a 2-terminal-pair bridge to a 4-terminal-pair bridge for increased range and precision in impedance measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new 4-terminal-pair bridge, capable of a relative uncertainty of 1 in 10/sup 9/, has been constructed at NIST by converting a 2-terminal pair bridge. The conversion requires only addition of components which are easily removed if 2-pair measurements are to be made. The design and testing of this bridge are described.

articleTitle: A determination of the SI value of QHR by the cross-capacitor in NIM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The determination of the SI value of quantized Hall resistance (QHR) by a cross-capacitor in NIM was completed in the spring of 1994. The SI value of QHR (i=1) was found to be R/sub H/=25812.8084(34) /spl Omega/ with an uncertainty of 0.132 ppm (1/spl sigma/). A CCC system is also being developed in NIM.

articleTitle: Multi-state radiometry: noise de-embedding and unterminating
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A noisy one-port device embedded in a noisy two-port is investigated from the metrology positions. The output noise power analyzed at different states of the two-port and the termination leads to defining the dual relevant issues of de-embedding and unterminating. A novel idea of multi-state total power radiometer for simultaneous measuring the reflection coefficient and the noise temperature of one-ports has been introduced.

articleTitle: A new solution of high precision wideband time-division wattmeter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new solution of the time division multiplier of the Goldberg type applied in the high precision wattmeter is presented. The solution is based on the method of compensating the systematic frequency error leading thus to the high performances of the multiplier even in the case when the conversion frequency is only 10 times the frequency of the signals to be measured.

articleTitle: Material characterisation from -160/spl deg/C up to 800/spl deg/C in centimeter and millimeter wavelength frequency band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A free space microwave measurement system has been developed to simultaneously determine complex permittivity and permeability of materials. The set up has been recently improved to permit high and low temperature measurements from C band up to W band.

articleTitle: DBR laser diodes for optically pumped Cs frequency standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This note describes the use of distributed Bragg reflection (DBR) type laser diodes for use in optically pumped Cs beam frequency standards. We have used a DBR laser at 852 nm as the optical source for the fluorescence detection of the Cs clock transition in NIST-7 and find it to be equivalent to the extended cavity diode laser.

articleTitle: Investigation of the offset charge noise in single electron tunneling devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The offset charge noise in metallic single electron tunneling (SET) devices fabricated on dielectric substrates was experimentally studied. On the basis of stereoscopic measurements of the low-frequency charge noise we show that the substrate makes an essential contribution to the total noise. We have observed that the intensity of the charge noise in SET transistors depends on the biasing dc current but is insensitive to temperature variations up to 300 mK.

articleTitle: A high accuracy reactive power and energy meter insensitive to frequency variations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The application of a frequency-controlled power-to-pulse-rate conversion in a high accuracy instrument for reactive power and energy measurement at power frequencies is described. Test results show that the meter accuracy is better than 100 ppm regardless of frequency variation of /spl plusmn/5% around nominal frequency.

articleTitle: Low-frequency measurements of the quantized Hall resistance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Measurements of the quantised Hall resistance R/sub H/(i) for i=2 and 4 have been made over the frequency range 0.4-6.4 kHz using a modified ac bridge. The results have been corrected for cable effects and the frequency-dependence of the standard resistor R/sub s/. The measurements indicate that in addition to a linear frequency dependence f there is also a linear dependence on source-drain voltage V/sub SD/ such that: /spl Delta/R/sub H/(i)/R/sub s/=/spl alpha/[V/sub SD/+/spl nu/(i)]f where /spl alpha/(i) and /spl nu/(i) are constants.

articleTitle: Present status of the NRLM superconducting magnetic levitation system for absolute determination of the magnetic flux quantum
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The NRLM superconducting magnetic levitation is based on the concept of quasi-static energy injection process, where the energy injected from external source to the coil system is equal to the sum of the increase in magnetic energy and gravitational potential energy. The levitation system uses a niobium coil and floating body with mass of 25 g. The measurement consists of two processes: (1) to increase the magnetic flux through the coil in terms of the Josephson voltage which we call flux-up, (2) to measure the coil current and the vertical displacement of the center of gravity of a floating body in equilibrium. By the repetition of these processes, the relation which we call equilibrium trajectory is obtained. The absolute value of the magnetic flux quantum is calculated in terms of the energy equation using the trajectory data. Hence, a quasi-static process is not vital. The levitation system has been developed at NRLM and the reproducibility of magnetic flux and vertical displacement in equilibrium at 0.1 ppm level was confirmed including Meissner effect of the superconductive material. In this paper, we report a recent improvements concerning mechanical energy determination as well as the changes to the electrical system.

articleTitle: Loading effects in resistance scaling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Power loading effects in dc resistance references are not well understood even for the most commonly used high precision standards. This paper examines loading effects and their contribution to the uncertainty of recent NIST comparisons of the quantum Hall effect and calculable capacitor.

articleTitle: Fast reversed dc: basic reference for ac-dc transfer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The improved design of the fast reversed DC source allows the measurement of thermoelectric effects in thermal converters of all designs and serves as a basic tool to control reference standards for ac-dc transfer. Residual effects in thermal converters are measured which are explained by nonuniformities in the heater material.

articleTitle: CCE comparison of ac-dc voltage transfer standards at lowest level of uncertainty
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In May 1996 the international comparison of ac-dc voltage transfer standards at lowest level of uncertainty, using a multijunction thermal converter as the travelling standard, will be completed. Intermediate results show an agreement of the majority of the participating laboratories of better than 0, 4 ppm at the frequency of 1 kHz, 1 ppm at 20 kHz, 1, 8 ppm at 100 kHz and 16 ppm at 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Optimized 1 V and 10 V Josephson series arrays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: By means of a new fabrication method and detailed design investigations we have been able to optimize the array circuits for the Josephson voltage standard. Even in very long arrays (4800 junctions in one stripline) a yield of 1 mV per junction could be achieved. The microwave power at 70 GHz required for the stable operation of 1 V and 10 V circuits could be reduced down to 1 mW and 10 mW (antenna input), respectively.

articleTitle: Saturation spectroscopy of molecular iodine at 532 nm by Nd:YAG lasers and their application for frequency stabilization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Compact diode-pumped Nd:YAG laser have been used to study the hyperfine spectrum of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ at 532 mm by means of modulation transfer spectroscopy. The laser frequency has been stabilized to a hyperfine line of the iodine. A long-term frequency stability of /spl sigma/=7/spl times/10/sup -11/ for /spl tau/=100 s has been obtained from the measurement of the beat frequency between two independent iodine-stabilized laser systems.

articleTitle: A triaxis broadband magnetic field meter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes a magnetic field meter having an isotropic directional characteristic, suitable for measurements of perturbative fields that can have dangerous effects on biological systems. The instrument is characterized by a great sensitivity and frequency range from 40 Hz to more than 100 kHz.

articleTitle: A dual six-port with homodyne phase-sensitive detectors as new option of microwave network analyzer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper presents a new concept of the broadband dual six-port network analyzer with phase-sensitive homodyne detectors. The features of the homodyne detection process with DSBSC audio phase modulation are reminded. The paper also contains a description of the dual six-port analyzer system which is able to measure all scattering coefficients of a tested two-port.

articleTitle: Microwave behavior of ferrites: theory and experiment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The relative magnetic permeability and loss factor of microwave ferrites in the demagnetized state are determined near and above gyromagnetic resonance using low-loss dielectric ring resonators. This technique allows complex permeability determination on a single ferrite sample from 2 GHz to 25 GHz. The measured real parts of the initial permeability are compared with theoretical predictions of the permeability of a sample in the demagnetized state.

articleTitle: A broadband microwave correlation radiometer using a quadrature hybrid coupler
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A broadband microwave radiometer of differential type has been developed adopting a correlation scheme with a quadrature hybrid coupler of low reflection coefficient. The system can be composed of three sets of the microwave frontends in the frequency range of 1 to 12 GHz.

articleTitle: New structure for a six-port reflectometer in MMIC technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents a new structure for a six-port reflectometer which due to its simplicity can be integrated very easily in MMIC technology. It uses non-matched diode detectors with a high input impedance that are placed around a phase shifter. The circuit has been fabricated by the foundry GEC-Marconi and operates between 1.4 and 2.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Linking electrical with mechanical quantities through electro-mechanical resonance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The possibility of an electro-mechanical harmonic oscillator obtained by coupling two linear capacitive voltage-force transducers with a common floating mass is shown. Approaching a constant-charge operation, the system yields a very-low-frequency ac voltage related to mass through capacitance, length and frequency. A possible use in the determination of the Josephson constant or the Planck constant is also outlined.

articleTitle: A low thermal guarded scanner for high resistance measurement systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The design and testing of a low thermal guarded scanner developed to provide completely guarded switching when used with guarded resistance bridge networks is described.

articleTitle: Using DC nanovoltmeters for low-frequency spectral analysis of voltage reference standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: It is shown that low-frequency spectral analysis can now be carried out easily and cheaply with personal computers. This method was used to determine the bandwidths of DC nanovoltmeters and to provide clearer interpretations of the filter and statistical functions in these instruments. Once characterized, the nanovoltmeters were used to study the noise characteristics of standard cells and Zener-diode reference standards.

articleTitle: A comparison of power measuring systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An automatic zero power factor standard has been designed and compared to a digital sampling wattmeter standard. The agreement of the two power measuring standards at 120 V, 5 A and zero power factor is within a few ppm.

articleTitle: New type of microwave resonator sensors with waveguide below cut-off
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A model of a quarter-wavelength coaxial resonator opened to a semi-infinite circular waveguide below cut-off is presented. A full-wave analysis of the transition between coaxial-line and circular waveguide was used. The analysis was based on a mode-matching formulation. The circular waveguide is filled by a dielectric material. As a consequence, the parameters of resonator: resonance frequency, quality factor, resonance transmission change in relation to the permittivity of the material. The fully automated microwave system was developed and used for measurements of low-loss and high-loss dielectric materials permittivity. Good agreement between theoretical calculations and results of measurements were obtained.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of optically pumped Cs frequency standard at NRLM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The optically pumped cesium frequency standard was reconstructed to operate it as a working primary standard at NRLM. The performance and handling are expected to be improved and this article investigates the performance in detail.

articleTitle: Two-way time and frequency transfer using optical fibers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A two-way time and frequency transfer technique using SONET (SDH) protocol is described. The system has demonstrated stabilities of 10 ps in "loopback" configuration. Preliminary measurements on a system performing full two-way time transfer shows stabilities of better than 100 ps at 100 seconds, limited by flicker phase modulation.

articleTitle: Multiple target FMCW ranging by evaluation of the impulse response phase
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A microwave FMCW radar for precise ranging of multiple targets is described. The evaluation of the FMCW raw data is based on a fast Fourier transform (FFT). In contrast to customary techniques we additionally evaluate its phase. The phase ambiguity is resolved on the basis of the more approximate envelope evaluation.

articleTitle: The multi-state radiometer: a novel means for impedance and noise temperature measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A unique noise measurement system for simultaneous determination of the impedance and noise temperature of microwave one-ports is presented. It employs a multi-state total-power radiometer, and techniques of calibration and error correction. Good measurement accuracy has been achieved using a high precision radiometer fitted with a noise injecting circuit to excite the DUT.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of magnetic fields from stimulated peripheral nerves
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The detection and multipole current source analysis of the magnetic fields over the lower spine generated by the electric currents in stimulated leg nerves are presented. The measurement of the fields, of the order of 10 fT, was performed inside a magnetically shielded room with a 83 dc-SQUID system developed by the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt.

articleTitle: Improvements of Josephson voltage standard in national metrology centre (NMC) Singapore
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes the recent performance upgrading of Josephson voltage standard in NMC. It consists of measures to keep the frequency stability of microwave source within /spl plusmn/1 Hz, proper ways of shielding and grounding to minimise spontaneous step transitions during a measurement and methods to reduce combined uncertainty by 10%.

articleTitle: X-ray crystal density study on a FZ silicon crystal for the determination of the Avogadro constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The systematic errors for the determination of the Avogadro constant using a FZ silicon ingot for NRLM are analyzed by studying the silica layer on the surface, macroscopic and microscopic defect in the body, of the sphere and concluded Avogadro constant shows the discrepancies around 3ppm to previously reported numbers.

articleTitle: High accuracy analog Hall probe
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The Hall probe we developed is a miniaturized analog system, consisting of two silicon vertical Hall devices, current stabilizers, amplifiers and error-correcting circuits. The output signal is 1 V/T, with an error less than 10/sup -4/ in the ranges /spl plusmn/2 T, 15/spl deg/C to 35/spl deg/C, and DC to 10 kHz. The probe features high long-term stability, low offset drift and low noise.

articleTitle: Dielectric resonator antenna for material characterization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In this paper, we present a first investigation of a new non destructive method for characterizing materials based on the use of a cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA).

articleTitle: Probe noise in an optically pumped cesium beam frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The influence of fluctuations in the probe laser's output on the performance of an optically pumped Cs beam frequency standard is clarified The analysis considers the probe laser's flicker frequency noise. Requirements for probe laser linewidth and modulation frequency are derived from the calculated results.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the calculable high frequency ac/dc standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The calculable HF ac/dc transfer standard has been developed at VSL. An improved model which contains a more detailed description of the thermal element with the end disc and the housing, is presented together with measurements. The major result is a calculated shift of about 4000 ppm in the ac/dc difference at 100 MHz. Based on this model, a 2 V standard is under development.

articleTitle: Influence of the contact resistance on precision measurements of the quantum Hall effect
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The influence of the contacts on the precision of the quantized Hall resistance is studied in a series of high precision measurements. Deviations of the Hall resistance of up to 0.35 ppm from the expected values are observed if the resistance of one of the voltage contacts is comparable to the Hall resistance.

articleTitle: Improved Josephson array step selection methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The objective of a Josephson array bias circuit and step selection method is to produce a highly stable pre-selected voltage as quickly as required. The results of measurements on voltage stability and selectivity obtained with differing bias methods and circuit components are reported.

articleTitle: Low-frequency sine voltage reconstruction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This report presents a technique of LF sine voltage reconstruction based on a new method of sine voltage measurement. This method reduces itself to sine voltage-to-time conversion by comparing this voltage with known dc voltage. The derived time interval should be converted into code and then the ac voltage value is estimated by a specific algorithm.

articleTitle: High-current thin film multijunction thermal converters and multi-converter modules
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: High-current, thin-film multijunction thermal converters (HCFMJTCs) have been fabricated at NIST with heater ranges from a few milliamperes to 1 A. Multi-converter modules containing HCFMJTCs have also been constructed to measure currents up to several amperes.

articleTitle: UTC dissemination at CENAM (Mexico)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.With the aim of disseminating the Universal Time Coordinate scale UTC, (CENAM) Time and Frequency Division constructed, in collaboration with the NRC of Canada, a talking clock system. In this work the system architecture and new added characteristics are described. A description of projects for disseminating UTC CENAM using a telephone and a modem, and by means of a commercial radio station are also discussed.

articleTitle: The MSL measurement of Newton's gravitational constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.We describe the progress made to our measurement of the Newtonian gravitational constant since the 1994 CPEM. Changes to the apparatus include: a new suspended mass and torsion fibre and improvements to the calibration of the electrometer. This paper describes these changes and presents our latest result and its uncertainty.

articleTitle: International intercomparison of silicon density standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In order to obtain a more accurate value for the atomic mass unit u, and thus for the Avogadro constant N/sub A/, the reliability of silicon single crystals' density values obtained by different measuring techniques was checked by density determinations with four silicon spheres at PTB, IMGC, and NRLM.

articleTitle: Recharacterization of the Zerodur capacitor by intercomparison of capacitance at KRISS, NML and VNIIM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An intercomparison of capacitance at KRISS, NML and VNIIM was carried out in 1995, using two fused silica capacitors. From the results, the KRISS's Zerodur capacitor, developed in 1984 and calibrated in 1985, 1987 and 1991, was able to be recharacterized.

articleTitle: Determination of the errors for calibration of power density meters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes a precision calibration method, which was used for the calibration of a power density meter developed for the measurement of hazardous microwave radiations by the Department of Microwave Telecommunications of TUB. It deals with the sources of errors (effects of reflections of measuring antennas, multipath interference due to the reflection and scattering of energy from other object and the errors originating from the uncertainty of the needed physical parameters) and calculates the value of resulting error for the free-space standard field calibration procedure.

articleTitle: Measurement and reduction of alignment errors of the NIST watt experiment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The effects of uncertainties in the alignment of the NIST watt balance with local gravity and the magnetic field of the balance have been analyzed, and techniques for measuring all misalignment parameters have been developed. The systematic uncertainty in the watt measurement due to alignment has been reduced to 0.04 /spl mu/W/W.

articleTitle: Systems of the electrical units and the fundamental constants
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Various modifications of an electrical part of the SI (Le Systeme International d'Unite's) are considered. The systems are generated by fixed values of the electrical fundamental constants. Constants whose values were adopted since 1990 for current representation of the electrical units of the SI via the Josephson and the quantum Hall effects are considered as the constants of the systems. The relations between the systems and ratios of sizes of the units are also considered. Consequences for calculation of the units sizes in process of treatment of data on the fundamental constants are discussed.

articleTitle: Recent progress on the 28/29 THz CO/sub 2//OsO/sub 4/ LPTF frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In this paper we report recent progress on metrological performances of the LPTF CO/sub 2/ frequency standard in the 28/29 THz range, using OsO/sub 4/ molecules as frequency reference. Significant improvements of both short-term (7.10/sup -14///spl radic//spl tau/ for /spl tau/<300 s) and long-term stability (3.10/sup -15///spl radic//spl tau/ up to /spl tau/=4000 s) are obtained. The reproducibility (over more than one year) is about 4.10/sup -13/ at present time.

articleTitle: Bose-Einstein-condensation and prospects for precision measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Summary form only given. In the past year, within a few months, three groups have independently succeeded in demonstrating Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) in a gas of alkali atoms. Our initial experiments, on BEC in sodium, were done in an optically plugged spherical quadrupole trap. Since then, we have developed a dc electromagnetic trap, demonstrated BEC in this trap, and observed light-scattering off the condensate in this trap. The trap is stable, easy to operate, and provides excellent confinement, which is important for efficient and fast production of Bose condensates. These properties are necessary for a detailed study of BEC, and for possible applications of Bose-condensed atoms. In this presentation our results to date will be reviewed. In addition, we will discuss some of the prospects for using Bose condensed atoms for precision measurements.

articleTitle: A fully automated system for the characterization of standard reference resistors using the quantum Hall effect
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The authors have constructed a self-contained, fully automatic system for the characterization of laboratory transfer resistance standards. A novel feature is the integration of all elements into a single cryogenic system. The instrument allows direct comparison of standard resistors with the quantum Hall resistance in GaAs/GaAlAs heterostructures. At low temperature the Hall voltage exhibits plateaux of constant value as the external magnetic field is increased, corresponding to a quantum Hall resistance equal to h/e/sup 2/n, where h is Planck's constant, e the electron charge and n an integer. The resistance of the transfer standard can therefore be determined from fundamental physical constants. The system comprises a /sup 3/He insert capable of producing temperatures down to 300 mK, a 14T superconducting magnet to allow resistance plateaus of up to n=2 to be attained, and a Cryogenic Current Comparator (CCC) mounted in a common cryostat to minimise liquid helium consumption. Use of an RF SQUID as a null detector allows DC currents in the CCC to be balanced with a precision of better than 1 part in 10/sup 9/. The system operates under PC control using the LABVIEW programming environment.

articleTitle: High resolution spectroscopy of the hydrogen atom
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The two-photon spectroscopy is applied to the hydrogen atom to measure the Lamb shift of the 1S level and the Rydberg constant. We have deduced the 1S Lamb shift from the comparison of the 1S-3S and 2S-6S/D transitions. In another experiment, a very precise measurement of the Rydberg constant is being performed from a direct frequency comparison of the 2S-8S/D transition with a two-photon rubidium standard at 778 nm.

articleTitle: The high C-field Cs beam resonator at the Politecnico di Torino
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Cesium atomic frequency standard is under development at the Politecnico di Torino. The whole resonator is conceived to reduce a number of systematic effects which are difficult to evaluate at the 10/sup -14/ accuracy level in traditional schemes. Some new solutions such as C-field value, cylindrical microwave cavity design and state selection method have been introduced in order to meet this goal. The overall design guidelines and the first results are reported and discussed.

articleTitle: A new experiment to measure G by means of a beam balance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We are preparing a high precision measurement of the gravitational constant G, using a new technique. This technique is based on a flexure strip beam balance and an optimised mass arrangement. In this paper we describe the principle of this experiment.

articleTitle: The need and use of intrinsic standards in U.S. industry
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The need for improved primary standards in industrial laboratories has been evident for many years. To meet these requirements, new methods and/or standards had to be incorporated into the primary calibration chain. The paper will address the requirements and performance of intrinsic standards for DC voltage, DC resistance, length, temperature and frequency.

articleTitle: Comparative radiographical registration of local nonhomogeneous physical fields
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The autors propose the creation of radiographical structures for registering and visualisation of physical fields in radiography. The processes of registering, registering materials and methods for information processing and interpretation are discussed.

articleTitle: Automated guarded bridge for calibration of multimegohm standard resistors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The implementation of an automated guarded bridge for calibrating multimegohm standard resistors is described. A guarded Wheatstone bridge has been assembled with programmable dc calibrators in two of the arms allowing multiple ratios and test voltages to be remotely selected. Preliminary measurements are reported along with the balancing algorithm.

articleTitle: Amplification and generation without population inversion in two- and three-level atomic media in a strong polyharmonic light field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The paper deals with non-linear laser spectroscopy of atoms in strong polyharmonic quasi-resonance laser field. The main goals are a theoretical study of the emission amplification effects in two- and three-level atomic media without population inversion, a calculation of the generation parameters at adjacent transitions in such spectral regions and such media where it is impossible or complicated to create usual lasers, e.g. in the UV and X-ray spectral region. Theoretical calculations show that the amplification effects without inversion in polyharmonic fields are connected with atom emission during transitions between the quasi-energy states into which the usual levels are splitted under the influence of a strong polyharmonic field. There are also transitions between quasi-energy sublevels and usual atomic levels. Hence, generation is possible in the spectral region which does not coincide with the pumping region (e.g., in a three-level system). Some of these conclusions have been already checked experimentally. Supernarrow resonances in the atomic susceptibility spectrum are found out experimentally and calculated theoretically. This is a new type of nonlinear resonances which can be used to stabilize the laser frequency, to receive generation without inversion in twoand three-level media. On the basis of the experiments, it is intended to build new stabilized coherent emission sources in the media without population inversion in the UV spectral region on the atoms of alkali-earth elements.

articleTitle: Precise comparator for checking of group inductance standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A comparator for the intercomparison of a group inductance standards is described. It enables the independent measurement of inductance- and serial-resistance-differences of two inductance standards. Measurement ranges are /spl plusmn/10 /spl mu/H and /spl plusmn/200 m/spl Omega/ with resolutions of /spl plusmn/1 nH resp. /spl plusmn/20 /spl mu//spl Omega/. The comparator enables an intercomparison of GR 1482-H inductance standards at f=1 kHz. The uncertainties of the measured differences are smaller than /spl plusmn/10 nH and /spl plusmn/0.2 m/spl Omega/. The uncertainties are approximately 30 times smaller than the observed one-year drift of the inductances in the group.

articleTitle: Calibration of multifunctional and multirange measuring instruments-the method of functional blocks for choosing optimal calibration points
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The full calibration provides the most confidence, but there are many reasons why it can not be carried out at more complex measuring instruments. In this case it is optimal to find calibration points by the method of functional blocks (FBs).

articleTitle: Improvement on the "coaxial to circular waveguide transition" method for complex permittivity measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The method proposed by Nour-Eddine (1986) allows the calculation of the complex permittivity /spl epsiv/*=/spl epsiv/U+j/spl epsiv/" of a sample measuring the complex reflection coefficient /spl Gamma/**=|/spl Gamma/|/spl ang//spl theta/ of the measurement cell. The proposed improvement introduces a resonance based analysis which permits the calculation of the complex permittivity by measuring only the magnitude of the reflection coefficient |/spl Gamma/|.

articleTitle: A 50 ppm low current multi-stage clamp-on current transformer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.An electronically-aided multi-stage technique is applied to a hand-held clamp-on current transformer which enables accurate low current measurements to be made over a wide dynamic range of operation, 0.5% to 100% of rated current, for use in conjunction with highly accurate power and energy meters, and harmonic power analyzers. The clamp-on current transformer can be used to measure currents in the range from 1 A to 200 A with ratio errors of less than 50 ppm in both magnitude and phase.

articleTitle: Dielectric loaded HTS resonators as frequency standards and low phase noise oscillators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We assess the potential for HTS dielectric loaded resonators as practical frequency standards and reference elements for low phase noise oscillators.

articleTitle: Progress toward an AC Josephson voltage standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Progress toward a Josephson voltage standard for fast DC measurements and AC waveform synthesis is described, including a version with SNS junctions operated at 11 GHz. A bias control circuit that achieves milliampere drive capability, transient suppression, and submicrosecond settling time is used for fast, automated measurements of A/D converter linearity, squarewave synthesis at 400 Hz, and a test for subnanovolt accuracy.

articleTitle: An active electro-optical loop and dipole probe for electromagnetic near-field measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An active electro-optical dipole and loop probe have been developed to measure electromagnetic near-fields. For the assembly of the probes attention has been paid to the sensitivity of the probe, to the susceptibility of the probes to interfering electromagnetic fields and to their high-frequency behaviour. The electro-optical loop probe (1 cm/spl times/1 cm) has a sensitivity comparable to that of conventional loop probes of the same size, can measure magnetic fields up to 0.1 mA/m and has a linear dynamic behaviour of at least 60 dB. The electro-optical dipole probe (h/sub eff/=1 cm) has a sensitivity that is better than that of conventional dipole probes of comparable size, can measure electric fields up to 30 mV/m and has a linear dynamic behaviour of at least 60 dB. In contradiction to most of the reported near-field probes with an optical link there is no conversion of the antenna signal to a DC-signal which means that all the spectral information of the electromagnetic field is preserved. This makes these probes excellent instruments for diagnostic EMC-measurements.

articleTitle: Improvements in the NRC ac-dc transfer capabilities
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes upgrading of NRC ac-dc transfer facilities, test results using new calorimetric TVC reference standards as well as redetermination of ac-dc transfer for voltage measurement over the 10 Hz-30 MHz frequency range.

articleTitle: A micropotentiometer-based system for low-voltage calibration of alternating voltage measurement standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes a new ac-dc transfer standard developed at the National Measurement Laboratory. It enables calibration of ac-dc transfer and absolute ac voltage standards to be made in the range of voltages from 2 mV to 500 mV, with an uncertainty of 10 to 1000 ppm in the frequency range 10 Hz to 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Present status and future trends in planar antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In recent years, various planar antennas for individual subscribers have been rapidly developed. It has been predicated that the antennas have considerably potential applications on a wide variety of areas. This paper reviews the antennas for DBS (Direct Broadcast from Satellite) reception at Ku-band (12 GHz) and summarizes their future trends.

articleTitle: Digital impedance bridge based on a two-phase generator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A digital impedance bridge composed of digital sine wave generators and inductive voltage dividers (IVDs) designed for precision comparison of different impedance elements is described. It enables one to measure impedance from 10 /spl Omega/ up to 100 k/spl Omega/ in the frequency range between 100 Hz and 1.6 kHz with a relative uncertainty smaller than 50 ppm.

articleTitle: Near-field measurements in the time domain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The paper describes the peculiarities of the time domain measurements with the use of ultrashort pulses. The time-domain measurement technique for a arbitrary scanning surface is described. We show the results of measurements of a parabolic antenna and discuss advantages and limitations of time domain measurements.

articleTitle: Studies of hyperfine structure in molecular iodine
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A table listing hyperfine constants in molecular iodine, /sup 127/I/sub 2/, has been used to develop empirical formulas for predicting hyperfine constants. Programs for calculating hyperfine structure in /sup 127/I/sub 2/ and in /sup 129/I/sub 2/ are available at the INM and at the BIPM.

articleTitle: Two photon transition around 778 nm in cold rubidium atoms trapped in a MOT
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Two photon spectroscopy in rubidium is a promising tool in order to build an optical standard around 778 nm. The paper presents an experiment attempting to observe the two photon 5S-5D transition in /sup 85/Rb atoms in a magneto-optical trap.

articleTitle: Development of an RSFQ shift register for applications in RF noise power metrology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Shift registers operated in 'xor' feedback mode and utilized as pseudo random noise generators are very attractive for application in RF noise power metrology. The paper reports on the concept of integrated circuitry required, based on superconducting Rapid-Single-Flux-Quantum (RSFQ) logic, and realized in Nb/Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/-Al/Nb technology. Results of shift register operation are presented for clock frequencies up to 70 GHz.

articleTitle: Correction of the RF complex reflection coefficient using air-line impedance standards of arbitrary phase shift
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: If the method of correction of the complex reflection coefficient using air-line impedance standards is extended to arbitrary phase shifts, considerable deviations of the results from values obtained with the quarter-wave correction method may occur. The influence of various input quantities on the uncertainty of measurement has been investigated theoretically and experimentally.

articleTitle: High power microwave pulse measurement using resistive sensors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The power heads on a basis of resistive sensors for high power microwave pulse measurements were developed and fabricated. They was independently calibrated and compared with Russian (former Soviet Union) pulse power standard.

articleTitle: Grounding resistance measuring instrument controlled by a microcomputer and a bias magnetic regulator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The author has successfully developed a grounding resistance measuring instrument controlled by a microcomputer. The instrument can regulate the measuring loop current precisely by the bias magnetic theory of double iron cores and adopt a flexible software to eliminate the error. Tests have shown that the measuring error is less than 0.5%. The instrument thus satisfies precisely the IEC stipulations for measuring grounding resistance of electrical equipment.

articleTitle: The state standard of magnetic induction unit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An instrumental complex for reproduction, maintenance and transfer of the magnetic induction unit in the range from 0.05 to 2 T has been developed and researched. Homogenous magnetic fields of different values are created in a multiband electrical magnet. A special system for stabilization of the magnetic field provides standard deviation of the measurement result up to 1/spl middot/10/sup -6/. The nuclear-resonant teslameter makes it possible to measure the reproduced value with nonexcluded systematic uncertainty of 3/spl middot/10/sup -6/.

articleTitle: Power factor calibrator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A power factor calibrator, using a precise wattmeter as calibration tool, to obtain short and long term stability and accuracy, is described. By frequently applying auto-calibration procedure most of the parasitic factors are eliminated and the accuracy depends mainly on the wattmeter's error at zero power factor. The calibrator uncertainty of /spl plusmn/0.003/spl deg/ is achieved.

articleTitle: Progress in the measurement of lattice spacing d
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Experiments on the lattice spacing measurement have been performed with an improved X-ray and optical interferometer (XROI). Previously reported standard deviation of 0.16 ppm has been reduced to 0.04 ppm. A new value of silicon lattice spacing is reported.

articleTitle: Toward a space clock using cold cesium atoms: the Pharao project
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.We point out key points of a microgravity clock using cold Cs atoms. The main characteristics of the experimental set-up (resonator, optical set-up, ...) are presented. Preliminary tests of a prototype are performed in the reduced gravity of aircraft parabolic flights.

articleTitle: The study of photon induced quantized current using an STM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present a new study for developing quantized current standard. Operating a scanning tunneling microscope (STM) with periodical photon inducing electron tunneling provides a way to count electrons. Therefore, a fixed number of electrons per photon pulse cycle can be made to tunnel.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of 1064 nm Nd:YAG laser using Cs/sub 2/ absorption
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have observed the saturation absorption of Cs/sub 2/ molecules in the tuning range of 1064 nm Nd:YAG laser and measured the absolute wave numbers of 94 absorption lines. We have also stabilized the laser frequency on the center of the absorption lines with a relative stability better than 2/spl times/10/sup -12/.

articleTitle: Optical pumping of helium-3 at 0.6 T [for proton moment measurement]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report on details of the successful high field optical pumping of helium-3 at 0.6 T. This is part of the progress on an ongoing experiment to measure /spl mu//sub h/(/sup 3/He)//spl mu/B. This work is aimed at overcoming the limitations of water as an NMR substance for high accuracy magnetometry.

articleTitle: Beam-astigmatism in laser interferometry
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We developed a null laser interferometer capable of 10 /spl mu/rad resolution in fringe division for the measurement of the silicon

articleTitle: Precision resistor of reduced dynamic error
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The precision wired-wound resistor as a reference element is widely used in the analogue signal processing units of electronic instruments. Our investigation is focused on the thermal dynamic behavior of these components. Using the model described in this paper, a power affected deviation of 1 ppm of the resistance can be handled.

articleTitle: Transfer of electronic oscillator frequency stability to laser frequency: an all solid-state approach to laser frequency control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A laser with both narrow linewidth and stable frequency is demonstrated using a diode-pumped ring laser locked to an ultra-high finesse tunable optical resonator which, in turn, is locked to an electronic oscillator. A 1064 nm beam is reported with linewidth on the order of 1 Hz with center frequency stability given by the electronic reference. In this case it is less than 1 part in 10/sup 9/ per day. The entire system is compact and solid-state making it ideal for spaceflight.

articleTitle: Fluxgate magnetometer for low frequency magnetic EMC-measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Based on amorphous core material a new fluxgate magnetometer has been developed for measuring magnetic fields with frequencies up to 1 kHz. With a novel sensor design and novel readout electronics which provide the stabilization of the premagnetizing field the magnetometer has a resolution of 10 nT. Errors due to nonlinearity and frequency response are less than 0.1% over the specified frequency range.

articleTitle: The influence of Young's modulus on roundness in silicon sphere fabrication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Silicon single crystal spheres for use in accurate determination of the Avogadro constant are fabricated by optical grinding and polishing. Surface profiling of the deviation from sphericity of the spheres shows a strong cubic symmetry on the scale of 20-40 nm, which is well correlated with the orientation of the silicon crystal axes. This deviation from sphericity can be explained in terms of the variation of Young's modulus with crystal orientation.

articleTitle: Experimental progress towards new definition of the kilogram using scanning atomic probes and picometer laser metrology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present our experimental progress in using atomic probes to continuously scan atomic surfaces, in developing picometer laser metrology, and in picometer real-time motion control for our scheme towards new definition of the kilogram.

articleTitle: Proposed tests to evaluate the frequency-dependent capacitor ratio for single electron tunneling experiment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A precise measurement of the ratio of two cryogenic capacitors is needed for a capacitor charging experiment using single electron tunneling (SET) phenomena. To support the capacitor charging metrology a frequency characterization of the capacitors is required. To cover the frequency range from 1 Hz to 1 kHz, resistive and inductive voltage divider bridges are proposed. Preliminary tests suggest that the uncertainty with which the capacitor ratio can be evaluated is less than one part per 10/sup 6/.

articleTitle: The muonium hfs: uncertainty of theoretical calculation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Leading logarithmic corrections into the muonium hyperfine splitting (hfs) are evaluated. A status of theoretical calculations of the hfs is observed and main items of theoretical uncertainty are considered. A new term in the order /spl alpha/(Z/spl alpha/)/sup 3/ ln(Z/spl alpha/)/spl nu//sub F/ is obtained.

articleTitle: Measurement of the thermal expansion coefficient of a cryogenic all-sapphire optical cavity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present measurements of the frequency-temperature dependence of a cryogenic all-sapphire Fabry-Perot optical cavity to be used as an optical frequency reference. Measurements were made by tracking the frequency of the cavity relative to a free-running Nd:YAG non-planar ring laser. Measurements cover the temperature range of 5 K to 77 K.

articleTitle: AC resistance bridge based on the cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes a low-frequency AC resistance bridge based on a Cryogenic Current Comparator (CCC). A low-noise dc SQUID is used as a null detector. The bridge is the main tool to trace resistance to 10 k/spl Omega/, 100 /spl Omega/ and 1 /spl Omega/ levels from the quantum Hall resistance (QHR). The ratio of the resistors ranging from 1 /spl Omega/ to 10 k/spl Omega/ can be measured with an uncertainty of the order of 1 ppb. The bridge is typically operated with a PC generating a sinusoidal ac signal ranging from 0.1 Hz-2 Hz. Using a vector analyzer as a signal source the bridge is used up to 1 kHz. Both sinusoidal and pseudorandom signals have been used to verify the frequency dependence of the standard resistors against the QHR. At present, the bridge can be used to perform accurate calibrations only up to 10 Hz.

articleTitle: Spectral analyses used for fluxgate sensors with a computer aided measurement system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The behaviour of a fluxgate sensor using amorphous alloy cores in a.c. magnetic field was studied using spectral analysis with the help of an computer aided measurement system and an adequate software. The characteristics obtained are linear for frequencies up to 5 kHz in the range 0-1.6/spl times/10/sup -4/ T.

articleTitle: Characterization of an Ar/sup +/ beam from a high current ion source using a multi-segmented Faraday-cup
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In preparing an experiment for the accumulation of a weighable amount of gold atoms, a parameter study of a high current ion source was performed. A multisegmented Faraday-cup was developed for analysing the real two dimensional beam profile.

articleTitle: Cryogenic sapphire dielectric resonators: performance and potential
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Sapphire dielectric resonators (SDR) at cryogenic temperatures have been used to produce oscillators of exceptional short and medium term stability. We discuss the demonstrated performance achieved at NPL as well as potential long term capabilities of this type of oscillator.

articleTitle: Performance of the cesium frequency standards and intercomparison system in the time and frequency laboratory of the CENAM (Mexico)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The performance of the atomic frequency standards held at CENAM is presented along with a description of the high-resolution phase comparator used for their characterization. The frequency stability measurements for short and medium term are presented. The phase comparator is based on the double mixer method with a resolution better than 1 ps.

articleTitle: The hydrogen Lamb shift: self-consistant values
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The special difference of ns/sub 1/2 / state Lamb shifts /spl Delta/E/sub L/(1s/sub 1/2 /)-n/sup 3//spl Delta/E/sub L/(ns/sub 1/2 /), which is need for evaluation of experimental data, is considered. The general expression for any n is obtained.

articleTitle: High-stable, compact Nd:YAG//sup 127/I/sub 2/-laser system for precision measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The results of experiments on creating a two-wavelength frequency standard on the basis of a compact frequency-doubled diode-pumped Nd:YAG laser (1064 nm, 532 nm) are presented. The use of a luminescent cell allowed to create a very compact laser system with a long-term frequency stability about 10/sup -13/ to 10/sup -14/ averaging time of 60s to 1000s.

articleTitle: Ten-volt Josephson junction array voltage standard at ETL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A voltage standard system using a 10-V Josephson junction array has been developed. The uncertainty is 0.6/spl times/10/sup -8/ for measurement of the 10-V output Zener diode reference standard. A comparison of the 10-V array system with the conventional 10-V measurement system composed of a 1-V array and a voltage divider was performed through measurements of a 10-V output of a Zener. The result agreed within the uncertainty (/spl sim/1/spl times/10/sup -8/) of the comparison.

articleTitle: Calibration of AC amplifiers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new AC voltage amplifier calibration system is proposed herein. The complex error of the amplifier is determined and stored, making possible software correction with the results. This way amplifiers with less than 10 ppm gain error and less than 10 /spl mu/rad phase error can be realised.

articleTitle: Fluxgate magnetometric circuit for measurement of d.c. and low frequency magnetic field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The environmental magnetic field generated either by the Earth or by the human activity can be measured using a fluxgate magnetometer, by means of a sample and hold circuitry. This contribution presents computer simulations of this circuit operation.

articleTitle: Low-noise high-speed general purpose SQUID system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.We have developed a SQUID system with superior performance to most of the systems currently available. It combines a very low noise level of 3/spl times/10/sup -6/ /spl Phi//sub 0///spl radic/(Hz) with a high bandwidth of 10 MHz and a maximum slew rate of 5/spl times/10/sup 7/ /spl Phi//sub 0//s at 10 kHz, where /spl Phi//sub 0/ is the flux quantum. Due to its excellent performance the system can be used for various applications, for example, to build high-frequency geophysical measurement systems, test circuits for fast superconducting logic circuits, wideband picovoltmeters, and low-noise amplifiers for magnetic resonance experiments.

articleTitle: Optical frequency standard based on cold Ca atoms: phase coherent frequency measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have determined the frequency of the /sup 3/P/sub 1/-/sup 1/S/sub 0/ intercombination transition of atomic /sup 40/Ca stored in a magneto- optical trap to be v=455 986 240 493. 95 kHz with an estimated relative standard uncertainty below 10/sup -12/ using a phase-coherent optical frequency chain from the Cs atomic clock to the visible. This allows the realization of the meter by visible frequencies with 25-fold reduced uncertainty compared to previous measurements.

articleTitle: Allan deviation measurements of a cryogenic all-sapphire Fabry-Perot reference cavity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An all-sapphire Fabry-Perot cavity is temperature controlled in a cryogenic (/spl sim/5 K) environment. The cavity is used as a frequency reference to stabilise the output of a diode pumped Nd:YAG laser. The expected stability is discussed and Allan Deviation measurements presented.

articleTitle: Frequency metrology via quantum interference in two-photon excitation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Quantum interference in atomic two-photon excitation is exploited for optical demodulation, with phase-sensitive detection at /spl plusmn/12 THz having been achieved. By utilizing the atoms as ultrafast nonlinear mixing elements, a new technique for the comparison of essentially arbitrary frequencies over the range 200-2000 nm is presented.

articleTitle: Josephson voltage standard comprising the hybrid integration of a Josephson series array and a planar oscillator for 10 GHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A computer-controlled Josephson voltage standard is developed comprising the hybrid integration of a planar oscillator and a Josephson series array. The 10 GHz oscillator is frequency-stabilized with a source-locking counter. A series array has been designed and fabricated in Nb/Al/sub 2/O/sub 3//Nb technology providing 648 mV when operated in a test fixture at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Precision measurement of capacitance bridge ratios for standard transfer
