publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This testing instrument performs the ratio determination of the precision capacitance bridge's measurement with an accuracy up to 1 ppm. The 10 pF fused silica standard capacitor can be used to transfer the capacitance standard to other ranges of capacitance measuring on the basis of the determined ratios.

articleTitle: A 7-junction electron pump: design and operation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report progress in the development of a 7-junction electron pump for use in a new capacitance standard. Cross capacitance in the pump has been reduced with a new geometry of islands and gates. Stray capacitance and charge noise have been reduced by using a quartz substrate. With these and other improvements the pump has become a relatively easy-to-operate cryoelectronic device.

articleTitle: Ultralow frequency oscillator composed of three switched-capacitor phase shifters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An ultralow frequency oscillator is discussed in which switched capacitors (SC) are used instead of resistors in CR phase shifters. The oscillation was stable down to the order of 10 /spl mu/Hz. The oscillation frequency varied linearly with the clock frequency of SC. An automatic gain controller is also discussed.

articleTitle: Clearly resolved secular sidebands on the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ 674 nm clock transition in a single trapped Sr/sup +/ ion, and prospects for trapped ion frequency standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A pre-stabilised 674 nm diode laser has been narrowed by locking it to a high-finesse ULE cavity and kHz error signals have been observed. Confinement of single laser cooled Sr/sup +/ ions in a miniature RF trap has been demonstrated and micromotion reduction achieved. RF trap secular sidebands have been observed on the Sr/sup +2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ 674 nm clock transition. The implication of these results, and similar results in other trapped ion systems will be discussed.

articleTitle: Analysing multidimensional measurement comparison data containing occasional erratic points
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper proposes a method for analysing multidimensional measurement comparison data containing occasional erratic data points. The statistics described exhibit robustness to the effects of such points, while being relatively simple to understand. They are introduced pictorially to emphasise their multidimensional "spatial" nature before a more formal mathematical description is given.

articleTitle: An active high voltage divider with 20-ppm uncertainty
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A voltage divider has been designed which consists of a group of solid-dielectric capacitors maintained in a temperature-controlled environment, an external compressed-gas capacitor, and special electronic circuitry. The prototype divider has been constructed and preliminary results obtained to validate the operating principle and accuracy target. The principal innovative part is a feedback amplifier, complemented with an "open-loop" voltage source controlled from the high voltage. This enables achievement of a voltage ratio that is equal to the reciprocal of the capacitance ratio to well within one ppm without encountering dynamic instability problems.

articleTitle: International comparisons of He-Ne lasers stabilized with /sup 127/I/sub 2/ at /spl lambda//spl ap/633 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: After the adoption of the new "mise en pratique" of the definition of the metre in 1992, a wide programme of laser comparisons at /spl lambda//spl ap/633 nm, the most used of the recommended wavelengths, was carried out involving national laboratories and the BIPM. Twelve comparisons were made involving thirty-six laboratories, which, for this propose, worked in regional groups. Except for a few lasers which exhibited some malfunction, when the lasers being compared were adjusted to have the recommended parameter values, their frequency differences lay inside the standard uncertainty (2,5 parts in 10/sup 11/) given in "the mise en pratique".

articleTitle: Development of thin-film multijunction thermal converters at NIST
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper gives an overview of the development of thin-film multijunction thermal converters (FMJTCs) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). A historical perspective of film thermal converters is presented, followed by descriptions of the motivation, fabrication processes, physical characteristics and the electrical properties of the FMJTCs produced at NIST. Integrated micropotentiometers which incorporate FMJTCs and thermal converters, produced by an alternative fabrication technology using a CMOS foundry, are also described. The paper concludes with a report on the current status of the FMJTC project and future directions.

articleTitle: Precision measurement of AC voltage under 20 Hz at IEN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A method for precision measurement of AC voltage for frequencies lower than 20 Hz is described. It consists of a sampling voltmeter working as an integrating analog to digital converter and of a set of software programs. Comparisons with measurements made using the thermal converters of the national standard show differences lower than a few parts in 10/sup 6/.

articleTitle: Investigations on a prototype of high temperature superconductor cryogenic current comparator with a toroidal shield
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Studies are in progress towards a liquid nitrogen current cryocomparator able to reach uncertainties comparable with the ones achieved by the liquid helium cryocomparators. For the shielding the ceramic high-temperature superconductor YBCO is employed. To overcome the difficulties arising in machining ceramic materials to reproduce the shield geometry adopted in liquid helium cryocomparators, investigations are carried out on a shield prototype adopting: a technique to obtain the shield as a YBCO layer anchored to a metallic substrate: a suitable toroidal shape allowed by this technique and studied via analytical and numerical approaches.

articleTitle: Magnetometry and frequency references with coherent dark states
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The 30 kHz linewidth and extremely steep dispersion of a coherent dark resonance in a caesium vapor cell allows measurements of magnetic fields to about 10 nT in 0.1 s integration time, limited by stray fields. The narrow resonance should make possible a compact frequency standard. In a preliminary experiment the authors used a coherent dark resonance in a 2 cm long caesium vapor cell to measure magnetic fields with about 10-5 uncertainty. Two diode lasers (852 nm wavelength) were phase-locked onto each other with a 9.2 GHz frequency offset, corresponding to the frequency ground state separation of the two caesium levels. The difference frequency is derived from a stable tunable rf source. Absorption spectrum of the caesium coherent population trapping resonance for linear laser polarizations is illustrated; it is split into seven components by a magnetic field parallel to the laser polarization direction. The width of the individual lines is only 130 kHz due to power broadening. The steep slope of the resonance could be used to lock the frequency of the 9.2 GHz rf source. This would provide a compact frequency reference.

articleTitle: Modern computer-tools for EMC-analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The method of moments (MOM) has proven to be one of the most valuable tools for EMC-analysis. Extending this method by transmission line theory, considering distributed sources, in conjunction with the complex cable transfer-impedance, delivers the possibility to calculate the signal-coupling from an external pulse source to an equipment port under the screen of a shielded cable. By combining the MOM with the geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD, UTD) arrangements can be analysed which contain both electrically small and electrically large bodies.

articleTitle: A mobile standard of frequency deviation unit in frequency modulation signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A mobile standard of frequency deviation unit designed for the verification of reference and working instruments measuring the parameters of signals with angular modulation is described.

articleTitle: Measuring the molar mass of silicon for a better Avogadro constant: increased certainty
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Summary form only given. At 3/spl middot/10/sup -5/ combined uncertainty the abundance ratio measurements of Si isotopes in natural Si must still be improved in order for the uncertainty on the molar mass to become smaller than 1/spl middot/10/sup -7/. One of the problems are the isotopic effects which result from adsorption/desorption processes of SiF/sub 4/ in the ion source of the mass spectrometer. In earlier work, some adsorption of SiF/sub 4/ gas was detected when measuring samples of widely varying isotopic composition (in our case enriched /sup 28/Si, /sup 29/Si and /sup 30/Si isotopes). These were removed from the internal surface of the spectrometer by means of a chemical process and prior to each measurement. In the work presented now, abundance ratios of the Si isotopes were measured by applying measurement procedures based on the knowledge gained from newly developed adsorption/desorption models. The latter enable to perform measurements under proven conditions of absence of memory. The values as observed in 1994/95 were confirmed, which means that: 1. adsorption/desorption models developed are (quantitatively) correct to describe and predict isotopic effects at the 3/spl middot/10/sup -5/ uncertainty level. 2. The measured abundance ratio values and derived molar masses have acquired an increased certainty, now equal to a combined uncertainty of 2/spl middot/10/sup -7/ M(Si).

articleTitle: Optical frequency standard investigations on trapped /sup 171/Yb/sup +/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Single /sup 171/Yb ions are laser cooled in a Paul trap, using laser sources based on semiconductor diode lasers. Excitation of the potential frequency-standard reference transition to the /sup 2/D/sub 3/2/, (F=2) hyperfine sublevel of /sup 171/Yb/sup +/ at a wavelength of 435.5 nm is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A new algorithm for the reconstruction of bandlimited functions and their Hilbert-transformed
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents a new algorithm which allows reconstruction of a bandlimited function from its sampling instants which do not have to be regularly spaced and the recovery of the Hilbert-transform of the function. The method described enables reconstruction of the real or the imaginary part of the dielectric permeability by means of the Kramers-Kronig-relations. The new algorithm also applies to two-dimensional functions.

articleTitle: Josephson voltage standard cryoelectronic circuits in Nb/Al/sub 2/O/sub 3//Nb technology operating at low drive frequencies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new type of cryoelectronic microwave circuits in Nb/Al/sub 2/O/sub 3//Nb technology for the generation of frequency-scaled Josephson voltages is presented. The circuits consist of superconducting microstripline resonators with series arrays of Josephson tunnel junctions located on the rf current antinodes. The circuits are designed to obtain highly accurate Josephson voltages at low rf power levels and low drive frequencies. At present, we have observed Josephson voltages up to 0.66 V in a resonator circuit with 1456 junctions.

articleTitle: Iodine stabilized He-Ne laser at 633 nm with simple line-locking device and the intercomparison results
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper introduces a simple line-locking device for iodine stabilized laser at 633 nm. This device provides an easy way for user to identify the saturated absorption lines and frequency stabilization without any extra instrument such as an oscilloscope. The international intercomparison results of the lasers from CMS, PTB and BTPM are also presented.

articleTitle: Determination of the time-constants of thermoelectric effects in thermal converters using a fast-reversed DC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A formula for determining the time-constants of thermoelectric effects in thermal converters from FRDC-DC transfer difference measurements versus reversing frequency is derived. The influence of higher-frequency harmonics in the FRDC-waveform is calculated for shunt capacitances in the heater/range-resistor combination.

articleTitle: High-sensitive spectroscopy of I/sub 2/-molecule by a power-stabilized diode laser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A novel high-sensitive spectroscopy using a power stabilized light was demonstrated by a visible diode laser spectrometer. The hyperfine spectra of 5-5 band P(84) line and 3-4 band R(69) line of I/sub 2/-molecule at 657 nm were observed. The observed spectral feature is suitable for the development of a compact transportable frequency standard.

articleTitle: Mexican realization of a cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A Cryogenic Current Comparator (CCC) Bridge for the measurement of the quantum Hall resistance and standard resistors from 1 /spl Omega/ to 10 k/spl Omega/ was built for its use at the National Center of Metrology (CENAM) in Mexico. Construction details and operating principles of the system are described.

articleTitle: Antenna factors of dipole and monopole antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Antenna factors of dipole antennas in the frequency range 20 MHz to 600 MHz have been determined to an uncertainty of /spl plusmn/0.1 dB (95%CL) and of monopole antennas in the range 10 MHz to 100 MHz to an uncertainty of /spl plusmn/0.15 dB. This leads to an advance in the precision with which electric field strength of free-space signals can be measured.

articleTitle: High-stable microwave range generators and their metrological assurance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The intensive mastering of the submillimetric range has stimulated the development of both measurement equipment for this range and metrological assurance equipment for high-precision measurements of frequencies and frequency characteristics.

articleTitle: An experimental of frequency transfer using a geostationary broadcasting satellite
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An experiment on frequency transfer using TV subcarrier was made via a geostationary broadcasting satellite. The Doppler shift is corrected using the velocity vector of satellite which is determined by measuring the Doppler shift at four reference stations with cesium standards. The precision of frequency transfer of 10/sup -11/ was obtained.

articleTitle: Development and investigation of shunted YBCO bicrystal Josephson junction arrays for voltage standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Arrays of 365 shunted YBCO Josephson junctions on YSZ bicrystals were investigated under microwave irradiation in the K-band. Subarrays of up to 39 junctions were synchronized to the external microwave power at the temperature of 15 K. A step height for the first Shapiro step reaching 30% of the critical current of array were obtained. Such cryoelectronic circuits are feasible for voltage standards and high precision D/A converters.

articleTitle: AC QHE-based calibration of resistance standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A coaxial transformer bridge for QHE-based calibration of resistance standards has been developed. An 8-decade two-stage inductive voltage divider forms ratio arms of the bridge and triple-series connection of the reference QHE sample to the bridge is employed. Frequency characteristics of LEP heterostructures have been measured by comparing them against resistors with calculable frequency dependences. Two quadrifilar, Gibbings's type resistors with nominal values of 12906 /spl Omega/ and 6453 /spl Omega/ have been used in this measurement.

articleTitle: Wide band horn (ridged horn) calibration by the three antenna method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The gain of the double ridged horn for frequency of 1 to 18 GHz has been precisely calibrated by the three antenna method in an anechoic chamber. The error in the calibration is estimated as /spl plusmn/0.15 dB or less.

articleTitle: New possibilities for creation of optical sources with noise level lower than the quantum limit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Summary form only given, as follows. The results of theoretical and experimental investigation of a new type of amplified optical bistability observed in an active interferometer with saturated, absorbing, and amplifying, mediums at excitation by an external signal are reported. The behavior of amplitude and frequency noise, including quantum noise of such non-linear optical systems was studied. The observation of effective suppression of noise at three to four orders of magnitude in the regime of amplified optical bistability was carried out for the first time. A strong amplification of input signal at 4 or 5 order and an anomalous increasing of the interferometer quality of up to 10/sup 11/-10/sup 12/ are observed at that time. The effects observed open a lot of new ways for the creation of coherent optical sources with infra lower noise level for precise measurements.

articleTitle: Phase-coherent measurement of the hydrogen 1S-2S frequency with an optical frequency interval divider chain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have measured the absolute frequency of the hydrogen 1S-2S two-photon resonance with an accuracy near 3 parts in 10/sup 12/ by comparing it with the 28/sup th/ harmonic of a methane-stabilized 3.39 /spl mu/m He-Ne-laser. A frequency mismatch of 2 THz at the 7/sup th/ harmonic is bridged with the help of a phase-locked chain of five optical frequency interval dividers.

articleTitle: The method of summation difference and applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new calibration procedure for high-precision instruments is described in this paper, that make it possible for whole calibration of high-precision instruments on working state, independently of more accurate ratio standards. Besides two basic methods, which are reference exchange and reference substitution, calibration results are proved, and the errors of measurement analyzed.

articleTitle: Noise analyses on Josephson junction array voltage standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In this paper we analyse the influence of the microwave phase noise on the Josephson junction array (JJA) reference voltage in order to investigate the limit of the contribution to the error budget of a JJA voltage standard from the microwave source.

articleTitle: Precise measurement of the accuracy of 24 bit ADC by AC Josephson effect
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper reports precise measurement of the offset error voltage and non-linearity error voltage of 24 bit analog to digital converter (ADC) from -10 V to +10 V on the basis of 10-V Josephson junction array voltage standard system (10-V JJAVS). Characteristics of the ADC have improved with correction of detected localized raggedness of those errors.

articleTitle: Ultra-stable optical frequency reference at 1.064 /spl mu/m using a C/sub 2/HD molecular overtone transition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Recently we have developed a new frequency modulation technique for detection of weak resonances of molecules located inside a high finesse cavity. We match the FM sideband frequency to the exact splitting of the cavity free spectral range. With this method we are now detecting saturated molecular overtone transitions with very high sensitivities. The resulting excellent signal-noise ratio for these weak but narrow overtone lines has opened the door for realizing high quality optical frequency references in many spectral regions in the visible and near infrared. Here we demonstrate its potential by presenting our recent frequency stabilization result of locking a diode-laser-pumped Nd:YAG laser to the P(5) line of the HCCD (/spl nu//sub 2/+3/spl nu//sub 3/) band at 1064 nm.

articleTitle: A transportable Ca optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.We report on the realization of a transportable Ca stabilized laser used to disseminate the frequency of the Ca optical frequency standard which was recently measured at PTB.

articleTitle: Experimental thermal converter with quartz crystal temperature sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Design and features of an experimental thermal ac-dc converter with frequency output are presented. As a temperature sensor a bulk acoustic wave quartz resonator with linear frequency-temperature characteristic is used. A thin-film heater is sputtered on the edge of the resonator. The responsivity of the device is 300 kHz W/sup -1/. The short term stability of the output frequency allows an ac-dc transfer at the ppm-level. The ac-dc voltage transfer difference of the converter is smaller than 10 ppm at 3 V input voltage in the frequency range of 1 kHz to 10 kHz.

articleTitle: Iodine-stabilized extended cavity diode lasers at /spl lambda/=633 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Doppler-free saturated absorption features of the P(33)6-3 transition of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ at 633 nm have been resolved with extended cavity diode lasers. The optical frequencies of the hyperfine transitions have been measured using an iodine-stabilized 633 nm He-Ne laser. The extended cavity diode lasers used both intra-cavity and extra-cavity absorption cells. Allan-variance data and reproducibility measurements are reported.

articleTitle: Using spectral estimation methods for external problems of microwave measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Antenna pattern (AP) and reflection coefficient (RC) determination is one of the most widely occurring external problems of microwave measurements. It is very important to develop the means of antenna measurements in the presence of echo signals. For narrow band antennas in the presence of frequency dispersion, especially in the millimeter wave range, the time-domain pulse method has restrictions. It is more perspective to transform multifrequency data to time domain by spectral estimation methods such as the discrete Fourier transform (DFT), Prony method (PM), generalized pencil-of-function (GPOF) method, least square method (LSM). A multifrequency method of RC measurement in free space using transformation from frequency to time domain has been elaborated previously. This approach permitted us to measure RC approximately equal to -28 dB. But many absorbant materials have frequency dispersion, thus only single frequency measurement can be used. For both problems the aforementioned methods of spectral estimation are the key problems and some results of LSM are presented.

articleTitle: The introduction of Taiwan's automatic computer time service
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A PC-based system that controls up to 8 lines, measures the delay and transmits an ASCII time-code has been built. It will connect to any modem at speeds from 1200 bits/s to 9600 bits/s using standard protocols. The fluctuation of total delay is less then 0.5 ms. That is, we can synchronize the time system of the whole Taiwan island via the telephone network with an accuracy of 0.5 ms if we can measure the path delay of our telephone system.

articleTitle: A microwave two-way time transfer experiment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Comparisons of BSF time and UTC(TL) for time keeping have continued in Taiwan for years. A microwave two-way, time and frequency transfer experiment without using the spread spectrum technique performed between TL and BSF broadcast station is reported. The result showed that the stability was less than 5 ns.

articleTitle: Intercomparison of silicon samples from the Avogadro project
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The NIST lattice comparator currently assesses lattice parameter differences among carefully prepared samples of monocrystalline silicon with a level of imprecision near 10/sup -8/. This instrument has recently been used to effect intercomparisons among samples from laboratories currently engaged in direct optical measurements of such lattice period. Results reported here assist in global estimates of the current state of the art of these determinations.

articleTitle: Experimental confirmation of the accurate performances of an optical frequency divider and an optical frequency comb generator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The coherence and the accuracy of a cw optical parametric oscillator (OPO) as an optical frequency divider and an optical frequency comb generator (OFCG) as a sideband generator were measured. The accuracy of the OPO as an optical frequency divider was checked at the level of 6/spl times/10/sup -13/. The accuracy of the OFCG sideband generation was better than 7/spl times/10/sup -12/.

articleTitle: Determination of step number in DC voltage measurement using Josephson junction array voltage standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A method to determine the step number of a Josephson array by using two combinations of frequency and step number is studied and uncertainty analysis is given. The method can correctly determine step number by using a voltmeter with accuracy of two orders of magnitude worse than that required in conventional method.

articleTitle: Structural methods for accuracy improvement of ac-voltage measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This report presents some structures of measuring channels and corresponding algorithms for processing results, that allow to decrease major errors of traditional constructions of ac-voltmeters. In the report are also included additional algorithms and methods for other implementations in measuring systems.

articleTitle: Measurement of millimeter wave transistor parameters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents our investigations on a problem concerning measurement of parameters of millimeter wave field-effect transistors mounted on a lateral side of H-waveguide ridges. The necessary measurement procedures and calculation techniques are described. The extension of the method to optimum noise parameters is proposed.

articleTitle: Three-probe reflectometer error analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The reflection coefficient measurement error for a three-probe reflectometer was analyzed. The influence of power measurement error, probe location, reference coupler directivity, attenuator value and probe coupling on the reflectometer's useful frequency bandwidth was investigated using computer simulation. The useful frequency bandwidth for the reflectometer with commonly used parameters, was estimated.

articleTitle: 10:1 ratio transformer for capacitance measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A 10:1 ratio transformer has been fabricated as a part of key elements to re-establish the capacitance standard at ETL. From the results of the calibrations, the offset from the nominal 10:1 ratio of our transformer has been obtained as 1.6/spl times/10/sup -8/ for inphase and 8.15/spl times/10/sup -7/ for quadrature with the reproducibility of the order of 10/sup -9/.

articleTitle: Calorimetric measurements of microwave surface resistance at cryogenic temperature
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The measurement of the surface impedance is always difficult at microwave frequencies, especially for superconductors. We give a new method particularly suitable for thin films. It is based on a microcalorimeter whose thermal load is realized by a superconducting thin film that works as a bolometer. The measurement system has been tested in Ka-frequency band for classic superconductors.

articleTitle: A proposal for G measurement with a freely swinging pendulum
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.An experiment for G measurement based on a fibre suspended light pendulum swinging freely in vacuum is proposed. This seems to be a better sensor for gravitational metrology than the ones that have mostly been used and appears capable of yielding an accuracy of 10/sup -5/ on the determination of G.

articleTitle: NIST comparison of the quantized Hall resistance and the realization of the SI ohm through the calculable capacitor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The latest NIST results from the comparison of the quantized Hall resistance (QI-IR), with the realization of the SI ohm obtained from the calculable capacitor measurement are reported. Various systematic checks have been performed.

articleTitle: Experimental and analytical investigations of crosstalk between leaky cables
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The advent of microelectronics has made possible a wide range complex equipment to be used within a limited space. In such systems, coaxial cables are used as interconnects in closely spaced bundles. These conditions dictate that particular attention has to be paid to the interference caused by electromagnetic coupling between the cables so that improvements achieved by the use of high performance equipment are not nullified. Because of the mechanical constraints, however, the coaxial cables have to be flexible and hence employ braided outer conductors, which contain a large number of small diamond shaped holes which permit the TEM wave inside to couple outside and vice-versa. The objective of this work is to apply a new crosstalk model to describe this field coupling caused by the leakage from coaxial cables.

articleTitle: Dual 6-port ANA calibration with a single impedance standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A newly developed method allows dual 6-port ANAs to be calibrated with a single, known one-port termination instead of air line standards. This technique is especially useful for low frequency calibrations below 30 MHz where air lines cannot be adequately characterized.

articleTitle: The NPL 10 V Josephson junction array voltage standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes the work done at the NPL, UK to establish a 10 V standard based on an array of Josephson junctions. The system is described and results obtained with the system are presented. A preliminary uncertainty budget is also presented which shows the system to be accurate to around 4 parts in 10/sup 9/ (quoted at a confidence level of at least 95%).

articleTitle: New straightforward method of estimation of phase, amplitude and frequency for high resolution spectral analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new method of precise phase, amplitude and frequency estimation of multiharmonic signals (corrupted by noise in common cases) is proposed. This method allows one to precisely reconstruct a high resolution complex spectrum.

articleTitle: A transportable Josephson voltage standard based on high-temperature superconductors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A transportable Josephson voltage (1-10 V) standard on the basis of high-temperature superconductors (HTSC), built at VNIIM for widespread use, combining a high accuracy with small operating costs, is described.

articleTitle: VANA evaluation via a multi-state termination
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In a series of former papers, a number of applications for a multi-state termination in the microwave range were described. This paper will consider the application to the accuracy evaluation of a vector automatic network analyzer (VANA) in greater detail, and give experimental results. The technique was applied to a commercially available VANA and, over the frequency range of 2-18 GHz yielded the following results. In a simulated measurement application, the projected measurement errors were mostly below 0.001 in the magnitude of the unknown /spl Gamma/, although occasional errors of a half percent were also noted. In one case, however, errors as large as 10% were observed which indicated a serious but intermittent malfunction of the VANA. It was also possible to demonstrate the general stability of the multi-state termination and also to recognize a small instability in one of its states.

articleTitle: Determination of saturation parameter in iodine and precise molecular linewidth study based on frequency measurements of He-Ne/I/sub 2/ standard at 633 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new method for linewidth studies in a primary wavelength standard is proposed, resulting in the determination of the saturation parameter in iodine. In this method, based on variation principle, the linewidth information is obtained through comparison of the accurate beat-frequency data with calculation results, obtained for beams with Gaussian intensity distribution.

articleTitle: Optical transducer prototype for gravitational-wave bar detectors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A prototype resonant transducer based on a Fabry-Perot optical cavity has been developed. The resonant mass carries one of the mirrors of the Fabry-Perot cavity, while the other mirror is attached to the bar detector. If a Nd:YAG laser is frequency-locked to this cavity, one could then measure small variations in the distance between the mirrors by comparing the laser light frequency to the characteristic frequency of a second Fabry-Perot cavity. This optical transducer prototype could theoretically operate as a single-quantum-limited device thereby bringing the bar detector to its maximum sensitivity. Preliminary room temperature tests of this prototype are reported in this paper.

articleTitle: Optical frequency (wavelength) standard, based on group of He-Ne//sup 127/J/sub 2/ lasers with /spl lambda/=633 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.In the report there is discussed a group standard of primary standards for linear measures, compiled of three He-Ne//sup 127/J/sub 2/ lasers and instruments for measurements and registration, to keep and reproduce the operation of the standard of wavelength for interferometer measurements of length.

articleTitle: Transportable He-Ne/CH/sub 4/-CO/sub 2/-laser frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A transportable laser frequency standard at 3.39 /spl mu/m and 10.2 /spl mu/m was created. The complex consisted of He-Ne/CH/sub 4/ and CO/sub 2/ lasers. The first one was stabilized on 76 transitions of the F2(2)P(7)3 methane line. The third harmonic of CO/sub 2/ laser radiation was phase locked to the He-Ne/CH/sub 4/ laser frequency. Long-term stability of 10/sup -15/ was achieved. Absolute frequency of laser standard was measured with accuracy of 10/sup -13/.

articleTitle: Physical model for the collision in an RF-trap
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A simple theoretical model, which well describes the collision problem in a Paul ion trap in the presence of laser cooling and RF-heating, is established and confirmed by experiment. As an application, the preferable conditions of the mass ratio and the density ratio in the sympathetic cooling for arbitrary pairs of ions are predicted.

articleTitle: Fine structure constant obtained from an improved calculation of the electron g-2
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper will report a new value of the fine structure constant a obtained by an improved evaluation of the /spl alpha//sup 3/ and /spl alpha//sup 4/ corrections to the electron anomalous magnetic moment a/sub e/. This will lead to a value of a with a precision exceeding 1 part in 10/sup 9/ when new measurements of a/sub e/ become available.

articleTitle: Frequency synthesis in the submillimetric range with sub-Hz linewidth
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Work is in progress to build a new frequency multiplication chain for absolute frequency measurements at 30 THz. Results obtained in generation of signals with high spectral purity at 700 GHz are reported.

articleTitle: Portable E-field strength meter system and its traceable calibration up to 1 GHz using a /spl mu/TEM cell
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The newly developed E-field meter system is intended as a transfer instrument between a calibration laboratory and, for example, an EMC test facility to generate RF fields that are traceable to national standards. The system uses a flat miniature E-field sensor and software corrections for frequency response, linearity and temperature effects. The calibration procedure with a special "/spl mu/TEM" cell is described and an uncertainty budget is given.

articleTitle: Data acquisition system for low level signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes a data acquisition system for low level signals with isolated channels and high normal mode rejection. The use of the integrating ADC and digital signal processing resulted in the solution of much lower cost then traditional systems with the same precision characteristics.

articleTitle: Novel fabrication technique for single electron devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present a new method for fabricating multilayer single-electronic circuits with vias, crossings and reduced cross-capacitances. A single electron transistor (SET) was fabricated with this method and successfully operated. Its intrinsic charge noise, 3/spl times/10/sup -4/ e//spl radic/(Hz) at 10 Hz, matches that of other SETs.

articleTitle: Fabrication of precision quantised Hall devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Produces a series of quantised Hall resistors suitable for high precision measurements in fields below 9 tesla. Critical currents on both steps are in excess of 100 /spl mu/A.We have optimised the structure and treatment ofthe AuGeNi contacts to give four-probe contact resistance values of 2 m/spl omega/. These contact resistance values are amongst the lowest reported.

articleTitle: Absorption of I/sub 2/ in the spectral region around 670 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An investigation will be reported of single-longitudinal mode selection, oscillation linewidth narrowing and frequency tuning obtained by extended-cavity diode laser for application in a system for linear I/sub 2/ absorption measurement around 670 nm.

articleTitle: Moving-coil and levitated-mass methods to monitor the kilogram. Resemblance and dissemblances
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper discusses, in the form of comparative analysis, the moving-coil and levitated-mass setups from the viewpoint of their ability to monitor stability of the mass standards.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of He-Ne lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present our works on the frequency stabilization of He-Ne lasers which include frequency measurement of the iodine-stabilized 543 nm He-Ne laser and two-mode stabilization of 543, 612, and 1523 nm He-Ne lasers.

articleTitle: Transmission of an optical frequency through a 3 km long optical fiber: application to absolute optical frequency measurements in hydrogen
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A 3 km long optical fiber is used to connect two laboratories in Paris. We present the metrological properties of this optical link to transfer an optical frequency standard.

articleTitle: Experimental comparison of "load-pull" measurement systems for nonlinear power transistor characterization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Load-pull measurements are essential to characterise power devices accurately. This paper presents a comparison between two active and one passive load-pull measurement system. The experimental results obtained with a power MESFET transistor (1 Watt) are compared in terms of output power level and power added efficiency for various load impedances and input power levels.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity correction of the integrated time-to-digital converter with direct coding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A method and computer program for automated identification and correction of the nonlinearity error in time-to-digital converter (TDC) with 200-ps resolution, implemented on a single FPGA device is presented. The nonlinearity error is identified and corrected by the neural network trained with the fast Levenberg-Marquardt learning rule. Resulting nonlinearity was improved from 1.25 LSB (least significant bit) to about 0.12 LSB (24 ps).

articleTitle: Cognitive graphics tools for sensors simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The development of means of uniform representation of constructive outlines of mechanical value sensors (MVS) for various techniques of simulation is one of the main stages of simulating intelligent system realization. This formalizing process includes not only the description of the specific character of the MVS design, but also the decomposition of its constructive outline according to the chosen technique of simulation. The attempt of creating a graphical language of declarative type as intelligent means of cognitive computer graphics for representation and processing of knowledge about the MVS design was undertaken.

articleTitle: Study of self-point defects in highly-pure silicon
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Almost pure silicon crystals are essential for the production of the next generation of highly integrated electronic devices containing significantly less amount of self-point defects than commonly available material. For metrological applications this new material can open the door for a new definition of the unit of mass by a representation of a certain number of Si atoms.

articleTitle: The results of /spl gamma//sub p/' (hi) and /spl gamma//sub p/' (lo) determination based on R/sub K-90/ and K/sub J-90/ at NIM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The measurements of the SI values of /spl gamma//sub p/', K/sub J/ and R/sub K/ were completed at NIM in June, 1994, and the result have been published. This paper is as a supplement to give the /spl gamma//sub p/'(hi) and /spl gamma//sub p/'(lo) expressed in terms of R/sub K-90/ and K/sub J-90/. The results are /spl gamma//sub p/'(hi)=2.67515357

articleTitle: The measurement of G
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The measurement of G, the Newtonian constant of gravitation, is a long standing problem which still continues to provide a challenge to our scientific creativity. A brief review of the history of G measurements is given. Today, the nearly 1% discrepancy between the recent PTB (Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt) measurement and the "accepted" value of G is of considerable interest to the world of standards. The fact that the PTB measurement appears to be competently and thoughtfully done makes the discrepancy even more intriguing. Finally, a new free-fall approach (using g to measure G) is described. In this proof-of-concept experiment, an FG5 absolute gravimeter is employed in connection with a movable 100 kg mass that surrounds the dropping chamber. Little g is measured when the surrounding mass is located above the FG5's dropping region and then when it is located below the dropping region. The difference in these two measurements together with the geometry of the surrounding mass can be used to determine G. The status of this work and prospects for future improvements using this technique are discussed.

articleTitle: Implementation of modulation transfer technique at the IMGC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Preliminary results for the implementation of modulation transfer technique using a He-Ne laser at 612 nm are given. The performances are presently limited by the noise of the detector, which was designed to be operated at a frequency higher than the one used for modulating the saturating beam.

articleTitle: Determination of the fine-structure constant by measuring the quotient of the Planck constant and the neutron mass
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: At the high-flux reactor of the Institut Laue-Langevin in Grenoble, the fine-structure constant was measured with a relative uncertainty of 3.9/spl times/10/sup -8/. After publication of this value, the experiment was continued. The latest results are given.

articleTitle: Thin-film bolometer for the 3.5 mm coaxial line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new thin-film bolometer mount for the 3.5 mm coaxial line system is being developed. It uses a structured nickel film on a mica substrate as a resistor. The bolometer responsivity and the frequency dependence of the reflection coefficient are measured. The results agree well with the behaviour of an equivalent electric circuit.

articleTitle: Pressure dependence of metal foil based 100 /spl Omega/ precision standard resistors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.We report on the pressure dependent behaviour of 100 /spl Omega/ precision standard resistors which had been fabricated on the basis of metal foil resistors (type MC 3020, Krasnodarsky ZIP, Russia). The measurements were performed in the range 900 to 1100 hPa using a temperature regulated pressure cell.

articleTitle: Saturated dispersion spectroscopy of the OsO/sub 4/. Application to high precision optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Optical double-frequency phase comparator is proposed for detection of sub-Doppler saturated dispersion resonances of the OsO/sub 4/-absorber. This technique exhibits high sensitivity and small dependence of the background on the optical geometry. Experimental comparison of the phase resonances with normal Lamb-dip is presented.

articleTitle: A noise-adaptive digital null detector
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes a digital null detector which is able to detect sinusoidal signals in the presence of correlated noise. It is therefore well suited for applications with digital signal generators. Measurement uncertainties on a prototype were seen to be up to six times smaller than on comparable lock-in algorithm-based null detectors.

articleTitle: RF-DC differences of micropotentiometers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Various sources of RF-DC differences of a micropotentiometer (/spl mu/pot) are analyzed and calculated, and the results agree well with the experiments. New design reduces the RF-DC differences of /spl mu/pot significantly. Observations show good stability over a 20-year period, which makes /spl mu/pots suitable as primary RF standards in the microvolt and millivolt ranges.

articleTitle: Phase differential frequency converters in precision apparatus of phase shift and power factor measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents a description of a phase differential converter with repeated frequency displacement allowing in the assembly with the sample voltage divider, "current-voltage" converter and digital compensation phasemeter working at the fixed frequency. This raises considerably the phase shift measuring precision and the power factor in a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: Determination of /spl Omega//sub VTT/ using the quantum Hall resistance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes the maintenance and traceability of resistance in VTT. The bank of the primary standard resistors consists of four Thomas-type 1 /spl Omega/ resistors in an oil bath (T=20/spl deg/C), a Thinsley 100 /spl Omega/ resistor (100 /spl Omega//sub Thinsley/) in an air bath (T=25/spl deg/C or 31/spl deg/C) and a ESI 10 k/spl Omega/ resistor (10 k/spl Omega//sub ESI/) located in an air bath (T=23/spl deg/C). Both 100 /spl Omega//sub Thinsley/ and 10 k/spl Omega//sub ESI/ can be calibrated directly against the quantum Hall resistance (QHR) using a low-frequency cryogenic ac resistance bridge based on the Cryogenic Current Comparator (CCC). The cryogenic ac bridge is also used to trace 1 /spl Omega/ standard resistors from 100 /spl Omega/. All these standard resistors can be traced to the QHR within 10 ppb. The calibrations are mainly performed at 1 Hz but the frequency dependence of the resistors are first determined in the frequency range from 0.1 Hz to 1 Hz.

articleTitle: Cotunneling rate on harmonic drive and triangle drive
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In a single electron pump operated by harmonic drive and triangle drive, the cotunneling rate is calculated based the adiabatic and non-adiabatic tunneling model. The result shows that the cotunneling rate operated by the harmonic drive is larger than by the triangle drive in the case of adiabatic tunneling (i.e. low frequency) and vice versa in the case of non-adiabatic tunneling (i.e. high frequency).

articleTitle: On using high-harmonic technique for laser frequency stabilization on absorption lines of hyperfine structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The advantages of using the high-harmonic technique for laser frequency stabilization to narrow nonlinear resonances are discussed. Assuming the profile of a nonlinear resonance to be symmetric and the frequency modulation to be harmonic, the effects of the laser tuning curve and of neighboring lines on frequency offsets are estimated.

articleTitle: An algorithm for the least-squares adjustment enabling objective detection and rejection of discrepant items
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new algorithm for the adjustment of fundamental constants is proposed. The main feature is the modification applied to a limited number of data which are taken out according to a classification rule. Data values as well as their standard deviations are subject to modification. Our results are in fairly good agreement with the recommendation.

articleTitle: A treatise on equilateral hyperbolic function bridge
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new Bridge-Equilateral Hyperbolic Function Bridge (EHYP) is introduced. The bridge design is based on the theory of the Compound Ratio Network (CRN) and has a balance equation of Z/sub x//spl middot/Z/sub s/=Z/sup 2/=constant, where Z/sub x/ and Z/sub s/ are unknown and standard impedance respectively, and Z is the constant impedance in the CRN. The accuracy of the resistive EHYP bridge is estimated to be 5 ppm when the substituted method is used.

articleTitle: AC-DC resistor using a bifilar microwire
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: AC-DC bifilar resistors (6.45 k/spl Omega/, 12.9 k/spl Omega/, and 10 k/spl Omega/), consisting of a microwire and fused silica block, have been investigated and fabricated in order to extend nominal resistance, to improve stability and to reduce mechanical sensitivity. The resistors can be used as transportable standards for direct comparison with quantized Hall resistors (QHR) at DC and AC.

articleTitle: The development of the precise standard cell that can be upset down
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: It has been proved that most of the standard cells, which are made with special technology and are able to be upset, have the annual variations less than 0.6 /spl mu/V through long-term survey, transportation, upset and all kinds of performance tests. It can rapidly restore the original value after upset down and is suitable to be the transfer voltage standard for the comparison of two different Josephson voltage standards.

articleTitle: Analysis of the laser phase noise conversion by an atomic vapor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present theoretical and experimental studies of the influence of diode laser phase noise on the detection of the absorption signal in an atomic vapor cell, and we compare the noise of the absorption and fluorescence signals. Excess noise is observed on both sides of the atomic resonance.

articleTitle: A new power transfer standard, its investigation and intercomparison
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes a new thermal power transfer standard (PTS) developed through collaboration between VNIIM (Russia) and KRISS (Korea). Error components of the standard were evaluated in Russia, Korea and Australia (NML). Also, an intercomparison between this PTS and NML's power standard was performed. The difference between the two standards at 53 Hz did not exceed 7 ppm of apparent power at any power factor.

articleTitle: Thermal expansion coefficient and compressibility of single crystal silicon
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Accurately known values of material properties for single crystals of silicon are necessary, to apply corrections in a planned high precision determination of Avogadro's constant. Measurements of the coefficient of thermal expansion and of the compressibility of silicon are performed by interferometry in the range from vacuum to atmospheric pressure and from 15/spl deg/C to 25/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Improvements in three-terminal thermoconverter technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.A progress in three-terminal thermoconverter (TTTC) sensor and corresponding power measurement technique is described. Thermal and electrical models of sensor microsystems were developed to optimise construction and minimise residual parameters affecting power conversion accuracy.

articleTitle: Precise laser spectroscopy of hydrogen and singly-ionized helium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have measured the hydrogen 1S Lamb shift to be 8,172,827(51) kHz, the most precise value for any Lamb shift. The result is in reasonable agreement with the predictions of quantum electrodynamics (QED), although its interpretation as a test of QED is limited by the uncertainty in the proton charge radius. A measurement of the He/sup +/(2S) Lamb shift by laser spectroscopy can bypass this limitation and investigate a nine standard deviation discrepancy between theory and experiment for this Lamb shift.

articleTitle: Shift of the Cs hyperfine transition frequency due to thermal radiation: experimental verification
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.It was observed that thermal radiation emitted from a black surface surrounding the atomic beam of a caesium atomic clock leads to a decrease of the clock transition frequency when the black surface is heated to about 470 K. The magnitude of the observed effect is in agreement with previous theoretical predictions at the level of the present stage of the evaluation of the experimental data.

articleTitle: Fabrication of single-electron tunneling devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have fabricated very small Al/AlO/sub x//Al junctions connected in series using electron-beam lithography and double-angle evaporation techniques. The average junction area is obtained to be 150/spl times/150 nm/sup 2/.

articleTitle: Second-harmonic generation at 1560 nm using a KNbO/sub 3/ crystal in a resonant ring cavity for frequency-locking to a rubidium D/sub 2/-line component
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The second harmonic of a 1560 nm DFB laser is generated in a KNbO/sub 3/ crystal placed in a resonant ring resonator. The laser is frequency stabilized using the optical feedback from the counterpropagating mode of the cavity. A second-harmonic signal of 0.38 /spl mu/W is produced and used to observe the /sup 87/Rb absorption profile.

articleTitle: A new experiment on the muon anomalous magnetic moment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.At the Brookhaven National Laboratory a new experiment is being set up to determine the muon's magnetic g-factor anomaly to 0.35 ppm relative accuracy which at this level may contain contributions from physics beyond the Standard Model and promises a clean test of the renormalizability in the electroweak interaction.

articleTitle: Non-incremental interferometric distance meter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents an optical interferometer for non-incremental distance measurements based on a frequency-modulated laser diode. The presence of a suitable optical feedback enables to get measurements also beyond the coherence length of the laser. The system resolution is of 50 /spl mu/m over a range of 0.4 m at a working distance from 0.4 up to 1.5 m.

articleTitle: Accurate AC measurement of the in-phase component of DC standard resistances
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A guarded AC voltage comparator bridge has been devised for the precise measurement of the in-phase component of DC standard resistances over the frequency range 10 Hz-100 Hz. It is based on inductive voltage dividers with electronically increased input impedance. The AC behavior of the resistance standards maintaining the NIS Ohm, as well as the working standards of values 1 /spl Omega/ to 10 k/spl Omega/, were investigated using this bridge.

articleTitle: Frequency measurements of hyperfine components in the UHR Raman spectrum of I/sub 2/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Very narrow resonances (3.3 kHz HWHM) have been obtained by stimulated resonance Raman spectroscopy of iodine with a continuously pumped cell. This technique is used to measure frequency differences between hyperfine levels of the rovibronic ground state. Experimental and theoretical line shapes are compared and the accuracy of the measurements is discussed.

articleTitle: Set-up for 3-dimensional positioning of magnetometer sensors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.As the sensors of many magnetometers, e.g. SQUID-magnetometers, are not directly accessible, often their spatial location is known only approximately. To be able to position such sensors more accurately, a measuring system consisting of etched coils has been developed to determine the sensor location by means of magnetic measurements with a resolution better than 0.1 mm.

articleTitle: Scanning X-ray interferometry over a millimeter baseline
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new translation device has been developed at the IMGC to improve the measurement of the

articleTitle: A power comparator with high accuracy simple and inexpensive
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes a thermal wattmeter that measures ac power within 10 ppm (1 /spl sigma/) at power frequencies. The instrument relates ac power to dc standards. Its main achievement is that its few components can be separately evaluated and by this means its total uncertainty estimated.

articleTitle: Fiber-optic current/voltage transducer for power system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A bulk Faraday-effect medium and a Pockles-effect crystal are used to sense current i and voltage u being measured successively. A typical optical method and a specially-designed electronic unit are utilized to separate the i and u from the emerging optical signal. This kind of current/voltage transducer is expected to be practicable and to have excellent performance.

articleTitle: A precise microwave spectroscopy measurement on the muonium ground state: hyperfine structure interval and muon magnetic moment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An experiment is in progress at the Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility (LAMPF) to determine with high precision the hyperfine structure interval /spl Delta/v (to /spl sim/10 ppb) and the muon to proton magnetic moment ratio /spl mu//sub /spl mu////spl mu//sub p/(to /spl sim/60 ppb) in the ground state of muonium (/spl mu//sup +/e/sup -/). These precision goals correspond to increases in precision of /spl Delta/v and of /spl mu//sub /spl mu////spl mu//sub p/ by about a factor of 5 compared to present knowledge.

articleTitle: Computation of the relativistic frequency shift of a frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Comparison of the frequencies of primary standards calls for the computation of the relativistic frequency shift with an uncertainty lower than that implied by the accuracy of the standards. This computation is also required to establish an accurate coordinate time. The problem is addressed at several levels of uncertainty, valid for present and future primary standards.

articleTitle: Precision measurement and calculations of the Lamb shift in hydrogen atom
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Detailed analysis of systematic errors in measurement of Lamb-shift in hydrogen by the atomic interferometer method is presented. QED-calculations of the 2p-level decay constant and the energy of the 2s-2p separation are discussed. Experimental results are compared with high-precision theoretical calculation data.

articleTitle: Atomic trapping in a two-dimensional magneto-optical trap
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We could trap rubidium atoms in two-dimensional configuration using two pairs of counterpropagating laser beams in a magneto-optical trap. The trapped atomic cloud was line-shape of 10-mm long and /spl sim/1.5 mm in diameter along the crossing of the laser beams. The probe-beam absorption spectrum was observed and from which the number of trapped atoms was estimated to be about 1/spl times/10/sup 6/.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Josephson voltage standards of the Sveriges Provnings och Forskningsinstitut and the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Comparisons of the 1 V Josephson array voltage standard (JAVS) of the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (BIPM) were made with that of the Sveriges Provnings och Forskningsinstitut (SP), Boras, Sweden, in April 1996. The results agree within an overall uncertainty of less than 1 nV.

articleTitle: New multisize inductance reference standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Multisize inductance standards based on passive toroidal inductance coils from 1.10/sup -6/ to 1 H for the frequencies 40-1.10/sup 5/ Hz are presented. In the second part of the paper, multisize electronic simulators of inductance from 10 to 20.10/sup 3/ H are considered.

articleTitle: Computations of the accuracy of VSM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The accuracy of the measurements by vibrating-sample magnetometer (VSM) has been studied by the computations of the sensitivity function. The arrangement of the coils is important to approach a wide spatial-uniformity of the sensitivity function. The errors due to the directional displacements of the sphere are lower than 2% if the mis-alignments are controlled to within some specific values. The uncertain radius of the sphere is also an origin of errors.

articleTitle: An improved three phase digital recorder system for calibrating power instrumentation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes an improved digital recorder system which is being used to measure accurately voltage, current, active, reactive and apparent powers and harmonic quantities for three phase sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal calibrations. The system has been designed to be used in the laboratory at the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) or transported on-site for tests in electrical utility facilities. Preliminary tests have shown that for sinusoidal waveforms, the accuracy of the voltage and current measurements of the digital recorder is better than 30 ppm and better than 50 ppm for active, reactive and apparent power measurements (with respect to full scale). The accuracy of the system for harmonic measurements is related to the harmonic content of the test waveforms and is estimated for individual tests.

articleTitle: Low voltage standards in the 10 Hz to 1 MHz range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A step down procedure is described for establishing voltage standards in the 1 mV to 100 mV range at frequencies between 10 Hz and 1 MHz. The step down employs low voltage thermal voltage converters and micropotentiometers. Techniques are given for measuring input impedance and calculating loading errors.

articleTitle: New cell of precision microwave dielectric substrates testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: High-Q dielectrical materials are widely used in modern microwave technology. The control of the quality of their production is the most important element of both modern and future technologies. Among different means of control of the dielectrics material parameters, the cells based on the junction 'round waveguides/radial waveguides' proved to be the most promising ones. The control is carried out by comparing the computed or standard frequency values with the measured frequencies of the waveguide-dielectric resonance of that substrate region, which is in the junction region. Restrictions are imposed on the thickness of the substrate and the value of its permittivity. An improved structure which eliminates these restrictions is described.

articleTitle: A resistance network for verifying the accuracy of resistance bridges
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A novel resistance network for verifying the accuracy of resistance bridges is described. The network can generate 35 resistance values with ratios which can be calculated to an accuracy approaching 1 part in 10/sup 9/. The network has been used to assess the accuracy of a cryogenic current comparator bridge.

articleTitle: The evaluation of NIST-7: a new era
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have developed a set of evaluation tools whereby all of the known systematic effects are evaluated by means of leveraged experiments not involving, or limited by, precision frequency measurements. This both speeds the evaluation process and greatly reduces the "combined standard uncertainty, extending the operational life of thermal-beam technology.

articleTitle: A digital servo chip microprocessor designed for the cesium frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In recent years the digital servo system has been used more and more in atomic frequency standards. In order to study its performance we made a prototype of such a circuit and reported the results. Based on the investigations a digital servo chip microprocessor designed for the cesium frequency standard has been developed. Its features are described.

articleTitle: Study of the Michelson resonator dispersion of an absorption-cell multimode laser with a strong intermode coupling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Summary form only given. The goal of this paper is a theoretical study of the generation modes of a wide-band multimode laser with a Michelson resonator and an absorption cell with atomic gases in one of the arms, as well as an interpretation of the experimental results on the basis of this analysis. Having a strong nonlinear coupling between the Michelson resonator modes through an atomic absorbing medium inside the resonator (in one of the arms), it is possible to have the following generation modes: (a). Stabilization of the laser frequency in the absorption line center due to the supernarrow dispersion resonance at the average frequency; (b). Generation mode where the difference in mode beat frequency difference gives a narrow frequency resonance with a field narrower than the natural width; (c). Generation mode where it is possible to split the central mode; one of the frequencies tracing the central mode frequency of an empty resonator. The calculations explain a number of effects: absorption line splitting, presence of supernarrow resonances at intermode beat subharmonics, emission concentration effect near the absorption line. These effects can be used to work out new techniques of intraresonant spectroscopy having a high sensitivity.

articleTitle: The NIST watt balance: progress toward monitoring the kilogram
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Random uncertainty of 0.08 /spl mu/W/W in the NIST watt balance has been achieved by improvements in a velocity measurement using three laser interferometers and by the reduction of filter delays and electrical noise. The latest results of this experiment are presented.

articleTitle: AC voltage ratio meter based on HTSC SQUID
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have developed the AC voltage ratio meter based on a HTSC SQUID. The possibility to measure ratios of voltage signals with the uncertainty /spl les/10/sup -3/ dB is demonstrated. The signal measurement range was from 300 /spl mu/V up to 10 V.

articleTitle: General method for quantization error predetermination in digital measurement system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Digital measurement instruments and systems have the quantization error as a systematic error, since there is no way to eliminate it. The standard intention is to hold it below tolerable limit. The paper deals with the method how to predetermine quantization error if the A/D converter word length, the numeric processor word length, the D/A converter word length and the measurement data processing algorithm are given.

articleTitle: Power calibrator using sampled feedback for current and voltage
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A Power Calibration Source for periodic signals is described, which consists of digitally synthesized voltage and current channels, the outputs of which are controlled by synchronous sampled feedback. This system results in accurate voltage and current wave-form conformity and stability in amplitude and phase at high power levels, regardless of power factor or in-band frequency. The system compensates for errors in calibration normally caused by amplifier non-linearity and loading.

articleTitle: Directly coupled electronics for HTSC DC SQUID based magnetometer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A low-volume high-performance directly coupled electronics for the high-T/sub c/ DC SQUID magnetometers has been developed and tested. This electronics is based on a liquid nitrogen cooled preamplifier with the white noise level close to 0.25 nV/Hz/sup 1/2/, packed in the volume less than 3 cm/sup 3/ and results in a typical 3 dB bandwidth of about 1 MHz, maximum dynamic range 140 dB for frequencies up to 1 kHz and the maximum slew rate more than 10/sup 6/ flux quanta in second with a middle-quality DC SQUID sensor.

articleTitle: An optical frequency standard using laser-cooled and thermal Mg atoms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.The Mg intercombination transition is an attractive candidate for a future optical frequency standard.
