Results of a detailed experimental and theoretical study of Ramsey-Borde interferometry using both thermal and laser-cooled atoms will be presented. Presently a stability of 5.5/spl middot/10/sup -13///spl radic//spl tau/ has been achieved.

articleTitle: Analysis of the light shift effect in the /sup 87/Rb frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The /sup 87/Rb cell frequency standard, optically pumped by a laser diode, is of great interest in the development of high short-term stability oscillators. We report experiments performed on a rubidium cell prototype aiming at evaluate the transfer of the laser noise to the hyperfine clock transition via the light shift effect, which appears to be the main contribution to the observed short term frequency stability in this kind of standard. Pulsed optical pumping will also be examined in order to strongly reduce the light shift effect and to achieve the theoretical limit never approached up to now despite the strong detected microwave signals.

articleTitle: Accurate comparisons of quantized Hall resistances at 1.6 kHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Accurate comparisons have been made at 1.6 kHz of the quantized Hall resistances corresponding to different samples, different values of the quantum number i (i=2 and i=4), and to both directions of the magnetic flux density applied to the samples. Preliminary results indicate that the different quantized resistances are consistent to within /spl plusmn/1 part in 10/sup 7/.

articleTitle: RC-generators with very high cycle-to-cycle amplitude stability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Simple principle of a RC-oscillator with excellent short- and long-term stability and low nonlinear distortion is described. Mentioned features are achieved by periodic recovery of initial oscillation conditions in each oscillation cycle.

articleTitle: About the accuracy evaluation of the LPTF cesium fountain frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Summary form only given, as follows. A laser cooled atomic Cs fountain frequency standard is now in operation at LPTF. Actually, the measured frequency stability is /spl sim/2.10/sup -13//spl tau//sup -1/2/ limited by the frequency noise of the local oscillator. Measurements are currently limited at 2.10/sup -15/ given by the resolution of the H-maser. The preliminary accuracy, estimated at 3.10/sup -15/, is discussed. The advance of the 2D Raman velocity selection is given.

articleTitle: Walsh functions based algorithm for distance protection, relay characteristic in Walsh domain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A major aspect of the application of Walsh Transform to the electric ac circuits is the definition of the impedance involving an integral calculus. Using the technique developed by Chen that represents the Walsh series of the integral of a function, the equations of the electrical circuit elements in Walsh domain are derived. A new algorithm for distance protection based on Walsh functions decomposition is proposed.

articleTitle: 1996 CONFERENCE ON PRECISION ELECTROMAGNETIC MEASUREMENTS DIGEST [Front Matter and Table of Contents]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Presents the front matter and table of contents from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: 1996 CONFERENCE ON PRECISION ELECTROMAGNETIC MEASUREMENTS DIGEST - SUPPLEMENT II
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Presents the front matter and table of contents from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: 1996 CONFERENCE ON PRECISION ELECTROMAGNETIC MEASUREMENTS DIGEST - SUPPLEMENT [Front Matter and Table of Contents]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Presents the front matter and table of contents from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Saturation spectroscopy of acetylene molecule towards frequency standard at 1550 nm region
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have observed saturated absorption of the v/sub 1/+v/sub 3/ band of /sup 13/C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ using an intracavity cell. These narrow lines can be expected to use as a frequency standard at 1550 nm region. We also demonstrate it is possible to saturate a weak molecular transition using a fiber amplifier.

articleTitle: Radiated fields from unknown sources
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Preliminary results of electric fields radiated from an unknown source, obtained by measurements inside a TEM cell, in an anechoic chamber, and above an open site based on available theories, are analyzed to confirm their equivalence. Either one of these three can be recommended as the standard for Taiwan industry.

articleTitle: Microcalorimeter for 3.5 mm 50 /spl Omega/ coaxial transmission line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: At PTB a microcalorimeter has been installed for calibrating RF power mounts with 3.5 mm precision 50 /spl Omega/ coaxial connectors (PC-3.5) to be used as power standards up to 26.5 GHz. Two detachable inserts with 3.5 mm coaxial transmission lines for a twin-type microcalorimeter have been developed. Measurements of bolometer mounts fitted with PC-3.5 adaptors and of a PC-3.5 power sensor are described.

articleTitle: Quantized Hall effect standard for industrial use
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Reports on the quantum Hall effect resistance standard, created in IMS specially for use at industrial metrological laboratories. The standard reproduces points of R/sub K//2 and R/sub K//4 with relative uncertainty below 10/sup -7/. The apparatus is easy to use and cheap.

articleTitle: Experimental determination of the gyromagnetic ratio of the helium-4 atoms in terms of that of the helium-3 nuclei
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The ratio of the /spl gamma//sup 4/He//spl gamma//sup 3/He has been measured using a gaseous sample in the low magnetic field. The result is /spl gamma//sup 4/He//spl gamma//sup 3/He=864.02276(0.03 ppm), leads to a value of /spl gamma//sup 4/He=1760.78798(0.3 ppm)/spl middot/10/sup 8//spl middot/rad/spl middot/s/sup -1//spl middot/T/sup -1/ using 1990 recommended value of /spl gamma//sub p/'=2.6751542(8)/spl middot/10/sup 8//spl middot/rad/spl middot/s/sup -1//spl middot/T/sup -1/ and /spl gamma//sup 3/He//spl gamma//sub p/'=0.7617861313(33) of Flowers et al. (1993).

articleTitle: A new refractometer by combining a variable length vacuum cell and a double-pass Michelson interferometer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new refractometer with a variable length vacuum cell has been developed, where the refractive index of air is determined by measuring the changes in the optical path difference between the air of interest and a vacuum as a function of the changes in the cell length. An uncertainty of 4/spl times/10/sup -9/ in the index has been achieved.

articleTitle: The multi-state radiometer: an uncertainty analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The measurement uncertainty of the multi-state radiometer, the first instrument capable of measuring the impedance and the noise temperature of one-port devices, is analyzed. Diverse contributions to the uncertainty, related to the radiometer calibration and the measurement de-embedding, are thoroughly considered on the base of the covariance matrix determined for the measurands. Experiments made using the radiometer support the analysis.

articleTitle: Quantization test of a Hall device by ac measurements of the longitudinal resistance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The influence of frequency on the quantization of a Hall device has been studied through ac measurements of the longitudinal resistance R/sub X/. The measurement technique is described and preliminary results are reported, which are in agreement with the model adopted to represent the system.

articleTitle: Precision volume measurements on silicon spheres
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In the determination of the Avogadro constant N/sub A/, use is made of silicon spheres as volume-density standards, where volume measurements play a critical role. The experience gained at the IMGC is reviewed and new data are presented on the reproducibility of the results together with some preliminary data on thermal expansion measurements.

articleTitle: A simple automatic system for calibration of inductive voltage dividers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.An automated system for calibration of manual inductive voltage dividers (IVDs) with an accuracy of 0.1 ppm at 1 kHz is described here. This system is established to reduce the time required in calibration of IVD.

articleTitle: Sigma-Delta modulation and PWM performs high-resolution DAC for DC applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A high-resolution DAC is designed with a combined Sigma-Delta and PWM interpolation technique. The result is a high performance, low analog complexity, no missing codes DAC suited for DC applications like low cost calibrators and complex instrument control.

articleTitle: A signal approach analysis of the Ramsey pattern in a cesium beam frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In this paper we show that the measurement of one Ramsey pattern permit us to estimate the microwave (MW) power very precisely, to calculate some of the effects that influence the accuracy of the standard without using the time of flight (TOF) distribution and to evaluate the TOF distribution very simply.

articleTitle: A compact transportable Josephson voltage standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The development of a compact, portable 10 V Josephson calibration system is described. Its accuracy at 10 V is expected to be 0.02 ppm. Its weight and volume are reduced by more than a factor of three compared to laboratory systems. The new system will replace travelling voltage standards used within several NASA and DOE standards laboratories.

articleTitle: An AC current source for capacitance-based displacement measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A 100 kHz bandwidth AC current generator used to monitor displacements by means of capacitive sensors is described. The displacement signal, linearly related to the capacitive sensor admittance, is monitored in 1 kHz bandwidth with an accuracy of 4*10/sup -4/ by means of a wideband high impedance buffer circuit. Performance and applications are discussed.

articleTitle: The double Josephson junction as a sub-single-electron-charge electrometer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The small-capacitance superconducting two-junction system shunted as a whole by a small-size resistor (R/sub S//spl Lt/R/sub Q//spl equiv/h/4e/sup 2//spl equiv/6.47 k/spl Omega/) has been analyzed. The sensitivity of the device to variations of the polarization charge Q/sub 0/ on the common electrode (island) is calculated.

articleTitle: Calculation of Kramers-Kronig relations with conjugated sampling series
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The real component /spl epsi/' and the imaginary component /spl epsi/'' of the dielectric permeability /spl epsi/ are interdependent by the Kramers-Kronig relations. In this paper the behaviour of the conjugated sampling series is examined. The limits of the applicability of the conjugated sampling series are described.

articleTitle: Interferometric cross check of two recommended wavelength standards at 633 nm and 657 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The wavelength standards at 633 nm and 657 nm in the visible part of the spectrum are characterized by most accurate frequency values obtained by frequency chain measurements. A cross check has been performed by an interferometric wavelength comparison and agreement was found within 3.8/spl middot/10/sup -11/ which demonstrates the applicability of both methods for a consistent wavelength scale.

articleTitle: Velocity distributions from the Fourier transforms of Ramsey line shapes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The Fourier transform method is routinely used to find velocity distributions for the primary frequency standard NIST-7. The second-order Doppler shift is calculated from these distributions. Experimental and numerical tests of the method show that the shift can be determined within a few tenths of a per cent.

articleTitle: Frequency multiplication and mixing on InP and GaAs Schottky diodes in IR and FIR regions and their use for optical time clock
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.InP and GaAs Schottky-barrier diodes (SBD) were examined as nonlinear elements for frequency conversion in IR (30 THz) and conversion multiplier in far IR waves. In FIR wave region harmonics with number N=37 at a frequency of 1.63 THz and with N=27 at a frequency of 2.45 THz are obtained at GaAs SBD from a millimetre-band oscillator. Use of a submillimetre (SMM) CH/sub 2/F/sub 2/-laser (1626.6 GHz) and a mm wave oscillator (64.6 GHz) allowed one to observe a frequency difference between two laser lines of 1691.21 GHz with InP SBD and 146 GHz with GaAs SBD.

articleTitle: Results of capacitance ratio measurement for the single electron pump-capacitor charging experiment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report on a metrological application of the single electron tunneling (SET) phenomena: a precise measurement of the ratio of two cryogenic capacitors. Our measurement used a superconducting SET electrometer as the null detector for a capacitance bridge. We have achieved a 3-ppm level of imprecision in the measurement of capacitance ratio from 100 to 1000 Hz. We used custom-made cryogenic vacuum-gap capacitors, which have a leakage resistance of no less than 10/sup 19/ /spl Omega/. Further improvements can be made in the attempt to obtain an imprecision of 10/sup -8/ at lower frequencies, sufficient for the metrological measurement of capacitance or the fine-structure constant using an SET pump.

articleTitle: Dependence of Josephson junctions arrays characteristics on temperature and frequency of microwave radiation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents the results of the measurements of 1-V Nb-AlO/sub x/-Nb, Josephson junctions arrays at temperatures 4.2-1.7 K in frequency band 54-80 GHz. The measurement of the temperature dependence of the critical current, gap voltage and subgap resistance of junctions is a useful tool for the quality control of arrays. By the measurements of the frequency dependence of array response to the microwave radiation it was found, that this response often has a resonance or interference like character, which is dependent on the array geometry. At the temperatures lower than 3-2.5 K as well as at low frequencies 54-60 GHz and T=4.2 K a transition to chaotic state of arrays was observed at small rf-power level.

articleTitle: AC-DC difference of millivolt thermal standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The error sources of AC-DC differences of millivolt thermal standards-micropotentiometers (/spl mu/pot's)-and the step down calibrations of /spl mu/pot's from 20 Hz to 1 MHz are analyzed. The new step down method for sub-mV ranges significantly reduces the /spl mu/pot's uncertainty.

articleTitle: International comparison of the He-Ne/I/sub 2/ lasers at the Slovak Institute of Metrology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The summary reports on the international comparison of the HeNe/I/sub 2/ lasers 633 nm, held at the SMU in April 1994. Parameters of eleven lasers from nine countries have been compared, including that of SMU B2 laser, the vacuum wavelength of which represents the primary standard of length in the Slovak Republic.

articleTitle: Exploring the low frequency performance of thermal converters using circuit models and a digitally synthesized source
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Low-frequency tracking errors of thermal voltage converters are described and estimated using circuit models. A digitally synthesized source is used to confirm ac-dc differences in the 0.001 Hz to 40 Hz range.

articleTitle: Determination of the frequency dependence of the AC/DC voltage standard at IEN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper reports on the procedures and on the devices, some of them of new type, utilised at IEN, for the determination of the frequency dependence of the thermal converters that constitute the AC/DC transfer standard.

articleTitle: Development of a portable optical frequency standard with a small calcium cell
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Calcium atoms could be trapped and locked directly in a small cell (about 20 cm long). A high power injection lock diode laser being frequency doubled to 422.5 nm by through a nonlinear crystal KNbO/sub 3/, is used to trap calcium atoms in the "heart" of the cell. The trapped atoms will be probed by a narrow linewidth extended-cavity diode laser. The diode laser then will be locked to the calcium /sup 3/P/sub 1/-/sup 1/S/sub 0/ intercombination line at 657 nm. The direct cell trapping and locking method makes it become possible to establish a compact high precision optical frequency standard.

articleTitle: Optimum sensitivity of an externally shielded cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The sensitivity of an overlapped-tube cryogenic current comparator (CCC) has been calculated including the effect of an external shield. Dimensions of the shield, tube and pick-up coil can be optimised to give maximum sensitivity. Improvements in sensitivity by a factor of two or three are possible for a typical design.

articleTitle: Using radioelectronic devices of mm-wave range for measuring length of moving objects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The present paper is dedicated to the development of a mm-wave range radioelectronic device, which is intended for measuring the length of moving objects. The paper is also dedicated to methods of processing the measured results. The use of techniques of mathematical processing of a signal with the help of numerical methods and Chebyshev's polynomials, enabled us to obtain a high accuracy of results (moving objects length). These objects have different cross section sizes and speed of movement.

articleTitle: Frequency shift of iodine stabilized He-Ne laser at higher order harmonic stabilization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The frequency shifts of an /sup 127/I/sub 2/ stabilized He-Ne laser were measured at the 3rd, 5th and 7th harmonic stabilization using a digital signal processing lock-in amplifier. The observed harmonic-order-related frequency shift confirmed the previous theoretical prediction that the center frequency of the iodine molecule transition is higher than the corresponding optical frequency of the iodine stabilized He-Ne laser. Use of the 5th instead of 3rd harmonic stabilization would reduce the frequency shifts caused by variation of modulation amplitude, intracavity power and iodine pressure, and improve the frequency reproducibility of the laser standard.

articleTitle: Re-evaluation of error terms for meaningful and practicable antenna and EMC calibration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Electromagnetic field calibrations are always influenced by boundary conditions. Boundaries are established by imperfections (e.g. cables, finite ground-plane, absorber walls) and by the measurement definition (source/spl rlhar2/detector coupling, ground-plane). A detailed discussion of coupling effects between undesirable boundaries and the measurement set-up reveals unconsidered or underestimated errors.

articleTitle: A system assuring the measurement uniformity of spectrum and form parameters of high frequency signals in the Ukraine
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In the report the methods of the measurement uniformity assurance of the form and spectrum parameters of radiosignals and their technical realization are considered. From the choice of models and of the methods of measurement in the Ukraine and the CIS a system of metrological assurance has been constructed which includes: the State Standard of the factor of amplitude modulation unit and the reference means for the verification of amplitude modulation meters; the State Standard of unit of the frequency deviation in oscillations with angular modulation and the reference means for the verification of frequency deviation meters; the State Standard of the non-linear distortion coefficient and the reference means for the verification of non-linear distortion meters.

articleTitle: Cryocooled primary voltage standard system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A Josephson junction array (JJA) cooled by a 4 K closed cycle refrigerator (CCR) is demonstrated as a primary voltage standard system. The calibration of a Zener voltage reference by this system is shown to have an uncertainty comparable to a liquid helium based system. Such a CCR system will have applications in national metrology labs, as well as in the military and commercial markets.

articleTitle: Antenna factor calibration in 30-1000 MHz frequency range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes the field strength standard established using a standard antenna method in 30-1000 MHz frequency range at KRISS (Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science). Measurement results of antenna factors are also presented.

articleTitle: Laser microwave double-resonance experiment on trapped /sup 113/Cd/sup +/ ions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Ground-state hyperfine splitting of /sup 113/Cd/sup +/ ions has been measured using an RF trap technique. The transition was detected with a laser microwave double-resonance method in the presence of He buffer gas. We determined the splitting to be 15 199 862 858 Hz. The preciseness of the value was improved over that in previous data by seven orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: Resonant frequencies of microstrip patch antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A generalized approach for predicting the resonant frequencies of microstrip antennas is described for computer aided design applications. It is capable of predicting the resonant frequencies of arbitrary shaped patch antennas. The approach has been validated for triangular, hexagonal, elliptical and rectangular microstrip antennas. The present work can also be used for measuring dielectric properties of slab-type materials.

articleTitle: Microchip design for Josephson-array in epitaxial structures Nb//spl alpha/-Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.In this paper the ways for improving the voltage standard based on the Josephson effect are reported. Problems concerning the reproducibility of the Josephson long-lived voltage steps in the circuits to be used in the voltage standards and other applications are considered. This problem is minimized by a new microchip design based on the hetero-epitaxial structure Nb on sapphire.

articleTitle: High Tc harmonic mixer applied to Josephson junction array voltage standard at NIM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.High Tc superconducting (YBCO) Josephson junction harmonic mixer has been used to improve the spectrum purity of the microwave source in the JJAVS at NIM. Compare with the microwave source using source locking counter EIP 578B, the spectrum purity of the microwave source has been improved significantly from -25 dBc/Hz (offset /spl plusmn/500 kHz) to -58 dBc/Hz (offset /spl plusmn/10 kHz). Therefore, the uncertainty of the JJAVS was reduced.

articleTitle: Optical selection of slow molecules in Doppler-free two-photon spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We observed a width of 280 Hz for a SF/sub 6/ line in Doppler-free two-photon spectroscopy at 28.4 THz. This is 25 times less than the 'transit width' and reveals the optical selection of slow molecules. This opens a new route for frequency standards in the infrared region.

articleTitle: A compact iodine stabilized He-Ne laser for inter comparisons
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.A compact iodine stabilized He-Ne laser at 633 nm has been developed. A specially designed mechanical construction and a short laser tube realize a short and light laser with good mechanical and thermal stability.

articleTitle: Thin-film isothermal dual heater thermal AC/DC converter with thermoresistive sensing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new thermal converter design for fast and accurate AC/DC transfer is realized by using thin-film dual heaters in isothermal configuration and aluminum thermoresistive temperature sensors deposited on a thin dielectric membrane. This design improves the signal to noise ratio of thermal converters which commonly use thin-film or thin wire thermocouples.

articleTitle: Primary standards for antenna factor calibration in the frequency range of 30-1000 MHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.There are two established methods for antenna calibration in the frequency range of 30-1000 MHz: The standard site method assumes ideal, calculable wave propagation conditions on an open-area test site with large metal groundplane. The reference antenna method uses a tuned half-wave dipole as a standard with calculable voltage at the feedpoint when exposed to a certain electric field-strength. The aim of our work was to minimize and precisely evaluate uncertainties involved in antenna calibrations using the two methods. In order to establish an accredited antenna calibration laboratory we took the following steps to obtain precision primary standards: We constructed an open-area test site that should exhibit wave-propagation conditions as ideal as possible. We constructed a set of precision, tuned, half-wave dipoles. We calculated site attenuation on an ideal open-area test site for our primary standard dipoles using the NEC-code. We finally measured site attenuation at 10 m distance in horizontal and vertical polarization. In the comparison of measured and calculated data we achieved an agreement of /spl plusmn/0.1 dB between 30 and 80 MHz, /spl plusmn/0.3 dB between 80 and 400 MHz, and /spl plusmn/0.5 dB between 400 and 1000 MHz for horizontal polarization. For vertical polarization agreement was within /spl plusmn/1 dB. We carefully analyzed the residual uncertainty and could dearly identify standing waves on the site by probing the field distribution along longitudinal and transversal axes. This influence can be taken into account by careful selection of antenna positions for the calibrations.

articleTitle: Laser observations of geodetic Earth satellites metrology and perspectives of development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Activities in the field of observation of the geodetic Earth satellites in the SSIA Metrology and of determination of the measurement uncertainty of a laser satellite range-finder (LSR) are discussed. The investigations carried out assume a new approach to determination of the LSR metrological characteristics.

articleTitle: A low noise and low cost YIG-oscillator in the frequency range from 2.2 GHz to 6.4 GHz for use in a high end microwave synthesizer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A low noise and low cost YIG-oscillator which is easy to stabilize within a phase-locked-loop has been developed. In order to achieve a good phase noise performance it has been simulated using only the linear scattering parameters of the transistors. Measurements on self-built prototype circuits have been made and show a good accordance with the calculation.

articleTitle: Measurements on curve-shaped horn antennae
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Results are presented of measuring reflectivities, conversion coefficients to higher-order waves, beam patterns, phase characteristics, gain factors and a number of other characteristics of stepped-curve and stepless-curve-shaped horn antennae. Measurements were taken both for the principal working wave and for wavelength variations to either side. A six-step pyramidal horn with dissimilar input-output cross-sections, showing optimum reflectivity, was taken as a sample to measure stepped-curved horn antenna characteristics. The obtained results matched well with the expected ones.

articleTitle: Environmental effects on errors in two-way time transfer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have investigated errors in two-way time transfer due to environmental fluctuations in temperature and power levels. The overall temperature coefficient of two Earth stations at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have been found to be on the order of 100 pS/K Sub-component temperature coefficients are as high as 400 pS/K. The errors in two-way time transfer due to variations in power levels have been measured to be as large as 12 nS. These errors are due to distortion in the pn sequence due to gain compression in the earth-station.

articleTitle: Precision frequency measurement of the clock transition in a Sr/sup +/ single atom with an ultra-stable diode laser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We are studying a single Sr/sup +/ atom confined in a Paul trap to produce a frequency standard in the visible region of the spectrum. The goal is to excite a clock transition of the ion at 674 nm with a diode laser and measure its absolute frequency. It is only possible to probe the 0.3-Hz transition if the diode laser is extremely stable during the measurement process which in this experiment can take several minutes to complete. Frequency stabilization of the probing laser was achieved with a lock to an ultra-stable Fabry-Perot cavity. The cavity was temperature stabilized and has demonstrated good long term stability.

articleTitle: Sensor with ferrofluid for magnetic measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new magnetometer with ferrofluid fluxgate sensor for measuring the intensity of d.c. magnetic field is presented. The electronic diagram with CMOS integrated circuits is described, as well as the ferrofluid fluxgate operation. The saturable fluxgate sensor is of the type of orthogonal coupling between the excitation and pick-up coil.

articleTitle: Intracavity iodine cell spectroscopy with an extended-cavity diode laser near 633 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: New technologies applied to visible diode lasers allow stabilization of an extended-cavity system using an internal iodine cell. Preliminary results at wavelengths around 633 nm are encouraging and show that such systems may some day replace the He-Ne lasers now used as frequency standards. The tunability of the diode lasers makes it possible to access iodine transitions which absorb more strongly than those usually used with He-Ne lasers.

articleTitle: Mutual inductance highly independent of primary winding position and ambient fields
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new design of high precision mutual inductor is described. Its main features are: immunity to ambient magnetic and electric fields and independence of mutual inductance of the shape and position of the primary winding. These results are achieved by using an electric screen and a hollow toroidal magnetic shield.

articleTitle: Measurement of complex permittivity and permeability and thickness of multi-layered medium by an open-ended waveguide method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The method of circular waveguide radiating into a layered medium is used for the determination of permittivity and permeability of materials. A better accuracy is obtained by the modelisation of an air gap between waveguide and material. The simultaneous determination of complex permittivity and thickness of the material is possible.

articleTitle: Stabilization of a 729 nm laser diode for a Ca/sup +/ optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.We present a 729 nm laser diode placed in a self-aligned external cavity and stabilized on a high finesse Fabry-Perot cavity in order to probe the high Q /sup 2/S/sub 1/2 /-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ Ca ion transition.

articleTitle: Refinements to the use of the NML calculable capacitor in relation to SI ohm determinations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: At CPEM'88 the result of a determination of the quantized Hall resistance in terms of the NML calculable capacitor was reported. Since then the capacitor has been modified, some systematic corrections have been revised and uncertainties have been reduced. A new determination has been carried out.

articleTitle: Standard time and frequency signal broadcast via INSAT-accuracy improvements using differential mode
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We describe the Standard Time & Frequency Signal (STFS) broadcast via the Indian domestic satellite INSAT. Under normal operation it is possible to achieve a synchronisation accuracy of better than /spl plusmn/20 /spl mu/sec. For users with high accuracy requirements we discuss the capability of the STFS broadcast to provide sub-/spl mu/sec accuracy using a differential mode. To our knowledge there is no other existing geostationary satellite based one-way time broadcast with this accuracy level.

articleTitle: Elevation plane scanning synthetic aperture radar: resolution and accuracy of point target localization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A width of surface swath, which is observed by a synthetic aperture radar (SAR swath width), is limited by the value, which is determined by a condition for lack of range ambiguities in the SAR-formed image (SFI). Existing techniques of SAR signals generation and processing provide SAR swath widening by special coding of transmitted pulses, by multiple beam (in the elevation plane) antenna system use in transmitting and receiving modes and also by elevation plane discrete scanning. These techniques' shortcomings are great volume of hardware and (or) reduced azimuth resolution. The authors of this paper have proposed a modification of the last technique.

articleTitle: A homodyne network analyzer based on the FMCW method and digital signal processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The use of the well known FMCW method for the construction of a vector network analyzer (NA) is described. The benefits of this new method are a very simple homodyne receiver, very fast measurements and the use of digital signal processing. The validity of the theory is proved by measurements of a microwave reflectometer.

articleTitle: The Josephson array voltage standard at the NMi Van Swinden Laboratorium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This contribution describes new developments related to the primary voltage standard of the NMi Van Swinden Laboratorium. The JAVS ofthe NMi Van Swinden Laboratorium is operated automatically, drastically increasing the efficiency of the measurement procedure while maintaining its best measurement capabilities. In addition, the development of a 10 V setup will be completed in the near future.

articleTitle: Measuring patch array antennas by an optically modulated scatterer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Two printed patch array antennas, a coplanar corporate fed 8/spl times/8 rectangular patch array at 12 GHz and a 6/spl times/1 circular slot patch array at 5.3 GHz, have been measured by a field mapping system using planar near-field scans with an optically modulated scatterer as the field sensor. The surface scans are made immediately above the patch array structure. They provide a good tool for diagnostic analysis of their working state of the antennas. The scans less than half wavelength above the surface give good results for their radiation patterns, which can be transformed to greater distances.

articleTitle: Asymmetry of resonances in iodine and unperturbed molecular transition realized by He-Ne/I/sub 2/ laser at 633 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new approach in studies of the line asymmetry has been undertaken in the commonly used wavelength standard resulting in precise measurement of the shifts arising from molecular collisions and from the iodine resonance asymmetry. The i-component unperturbed molecular transition frequency has been found to be 473 612 214 858.8/spl plusmn/12.7 kHz.

articleTitle: An HF/VHF automated microcircuit admittance bridge for operation in a -60/spl deg/C to +125/spl deg/C air chamber with milliKelvin stability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An electronically tunable admittance bridge is described which is self-calibrating and reproduces DC/LF measurements of resistance/capacitance to better than 2%, with a repeatability of a few microSiemens and a few femtoFarad respectively. It now is used in the 1 MHz to 160 MHz range, primarily as the measuring head in an air chamber for the evaluation of the aging and frequency/temperature characteristics of a multitude of crystal resonators, mounted on a transport rack. The 1 m/sup 3/ temperature chamber has a range of -60/spl deg/C to +125/spl deg/C and a stability of a few milliKelvin at any set-point in that range.

articleTitle: The materialization of the Metre at BNM-INM, the French National Institute for wavelength metrology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper summarizes the activities and the research projects in progress in the laser, wavelength and length group of BNM-INM, one of the French National Laboratories for Primary Metrology. They range from the search for new optical clocks to the transfer of air-wavelength references to calibration centers.

articleTitle: Measuring Planck's constant and monitoring the kilogram at NPL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.We are commencing measurements aimed at a definitive value for h with an uncertainty of about 1 in 10/sup 8/ and a target completion time of June, 1996. Many incremental improvements to the apparatus have enabled us to obtain a resolution of 1 in 10/sup 8/ (including the measurement of gravitational acceleration). Investigation of systematic errors is beginning.

articleTitle: Measurement techniques for electromagnetic interference testing of modern communication receivers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. The current rapid growth in the cellular market has already seen an explosion in the civilian use of interference agile modern communication receivers, such as Spread Spectrum (SS) systems. These systems are expected operate in electromagnetically dense hostile communication channels and the success of each system is measured in terms of its resilience against the Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) originating in the channel and the nonlinear effects in receiver front ends. In spite of this there is currently no established tools or procedures where interference effects are accounted for at the initial stages of receiver design.

articleTitle: Methods of EMC characteristics improvement in input microwave amplifiers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The results of work to improve input microwave amplifier EMC parameters are given. The original methods of theoretical and experimental investigations of amplifier EMC characteristics are outlined. Using these methods we design the EMC characteristics by reconsidering construction and changing of amplifier supply modes. Several types of vacuum and solid-state input amplifiers are considered.

articleTitle: Comparison of 10 V calibrations between KRISS and ETL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The results of an intercomparison of 10 V dc voltage standard calibrations between KRISS (Korea) and ETL (Japan) conducted from September to October in 1995 are described. A commercial Zener voltage standard (Fluke 732 B) owned by KRISS was hand-carried for the comparison. A preliminary analysis of the result is strongly implying the two 10 V calibration systems, both of which are based on 10:1 divider and l-V Josephson array are in good agreement within an uncertainty less than 0.05 ppm.

articleTitle: The molar volume of silicon
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Molar masses M and densities /spl rho/ of silicon in 1 kg Si almost perfect single crystals have been measured over the last several years to very small uncertainties in order to improve our knowledge of the Avogadro constant. Combining both is an excellent way to determine the molar volume of silicon. Small variations in isotopic composition and hence in molar mass must have the same effect on M as on /spl rho/: more of a light isotope (e.g. /sup 28/Si) will automatically reduce both M and and S values, but leave M//spl rho/ invariant. Since the three Avogadro projects (PTB-IRMM, IMGC-IRMM and NRLM-IRMM) used different crystals, it is worthwhile to review experimental values for M and /spl rho/ and determine our present best knowledge of M//spl rho/ the molar volume of Si in a single crystal. The (linked) improvements in the geometry and surface quality of the spherical artifacts and the measurement of mass and volume (hence density) as well as of molar mass, allow the testing of the hypothesis of the invariance of M//spl rho/ to reduced levels of uncertainty. The comparison of the relative standard uncertainties of M and /spl rho/ with those on M//spl rho/ reveal possible-albeit extremely small-systematic differences in isotopic composition in the various Si crystals used. This paper reports on that and indicates our present best knowledge of the molar volume of Si in single crystals.

articleTitle: Intrinsic Josephson effects in high-T/sub c/ superconductors-implications for future voltage standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: It has been shown recently that high-T/sub c/ superconductors are, by virtue of their layered crystal structure, a natural series array of atomic scale Josephson junctions. Do such intrinsic Josephson arrays have a future as voltage standards? This question is discussed in relation to experiments on the high-T/sub c/ superconductor Bi/sub 2/Sr/sub 2/CaCu/sub 2/O/sub x/ (Bi-2212).

articleTitle: Corrections of order /spl alpha//sup 2/(Z/spl alpha/)/sup 5/ to hyperfine splitting in muonium and to the hydrogen Lamb shift
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Corrections of order /spl alpha//sup 2/(Z/spl alpha/)/sup 5/ to hyperfine splitting and Lamb shift induced by the diagrams with radiative photon insertions in the electron line are calculated.

articleTitle: Enhancement of single mode selection efficiency of He-Ne and He-Ne/I/sub 2/ lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: For He-Ne and He-Ne/I/sub 2/ lasers, in case of natural mixture of neon isotopes, an influence of the isotope with lower concentration on longitudinal mode competition is observed. An application of this phenomenon is proposed for an enhancement of the single mode selection efficiency.

articleTitle: Frequency differences and reproducibility investigation on iodine stabilized He-Ne lasers at 474 THz (633 nm) with compatible system of third and fifth harmonic locking
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have developed a compatible system of third and fifth harmonic locking with computer control. Two lasers were stabilized with fifth harmonic locking instead of third harmonic locking, the frequency reproducibility could be better than that of the third harmonic locking.

articleTitle: Amplifier noise measurements at NIST
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has certified noise figure measurements near 0.6 dB with an uncertainty of /spl plusmn/0.05 dB. This paper addresses the error analysis and measurement assurance used for these measurements.

articleTitle: Power standards in millimeter range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The Power Standards in continuous frequency range from 37.5 to 178.6 GHz were entirely modernized and automated in 1992-1995. The main features, the principles of operation and metrological characteristics are given, including the power transfer, the comparisons and the long-term stability. For an independent control at the short wavelength end of the band a wide-band transducer is calibrated in microcalorimeter.

articleTitle: Investigation for high-resolution spectroscopy of the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2 /-/sup 2/D/sub 5/12/ transition of laser-cooled trapped Yb/sup +/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We drove the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2 /-/sup 2/D/sub 5/12/ transition of laser-cooled trapped Yb/sup +/ by frequency-doubled diode-laser radiation. The /sup 2/F/sub 7/2/ state, pumped by driving this transition, was deexcited by irradiation at 3.43 /spl mu/m, 638 nm, and 828 nm.

articleTitle: Change of the working temperature of the IEN primary group of standard resistors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The experimental procedure to change the working temperature of the IEN primary group of standard resistors and the results obtained are reported. After the change the resistors show an exponential drift with mean time constant of about 0.6 years.

articleTitle: Results of absolute frequency measurements with transportable double-mode He-Ne/CH/sub 4/ optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Results of absolute frequency measurements carried on at PTB in the 1995 year with transportable HeNe/CH/sub 4/ laser (Lebedev Institute, Moscow) stabilized over the resolved magnetic hyperfine structure (MHPS) of F/sup (2)//sub 2/ methane line (/spl lambda/=3.39 /spl mu/m) are presented.

articleTitle: Multitone load-pull characterization system for power and distortion analysis of microwave transistors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents a new load-pull measurement system for transistor characterization under N tone excitation signal where N/spl ges/2. The new set up uses an arbitrary wave generator (AWG) to generate the spectrum of any N desired tones to be applied to the transistor and a microwave transition analyzer (MTA) as a receiver. With such system, constant output power contours and intermodulation rejection (IMR) contours in the /spl Gamma//sub L/(fo) plane can be obtained. Using such system, one can experimentally investigate intermodulation distortion in transistors as function of their loading and the number of tones.

articleTitle: An isothermal method for coaxial microcalorimeter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An isothermal method is presented to reduce the thermal time constant of microcalorimeter. The method is a comparatively more efficient process of determining the effective efficiency of thermistor mount than classical measurement method. Using this technique with APC-7 coaxial microcalorimeter has substantially reduced the measurement time by a factor of six.

articleTitle: Sine-fit versus DFT-based algorithms in SNR testing of waveform digitizers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An analysis is given of the performances of DFT-based algorithms employed in SNR testing of digitizers, compared to sine-fit procedures.

articleTitle: A new magnetic field sensor based on magnetostrictive delay lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A magnetic field sensor based on the dependence of the magnetostrictive delay line (MDL) response on its biasing magnetic field is presented in this paper. Such sensor can be formed in integrated array measuring distribution of field along the MDL axis. Experimental results are reported concerning amorphous FeSiB wire MDLs.

articleTitle: Prompt (n, /spl gamma/)-spectrometry for the isotopical analysis of silicon crystals for the Avogadro-project
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The aim of the Avogadro-project is to replace the kilogram artefact by a high purity, perfect single crystal of natural silicon. Therefore, the isotopical compositon and the impurities of the single crystals have to be known with highest possible accuracy. The only method to achieve all this information without destruction of the massive samples is the prompt (n, /spl gamma/)-spectrometry. This method involves the analysis of the prompt emitted /spl gamma/-rays according to their energy and intensity after thermal neutron capture. The prompt /spl gamma/-energy ranges up to 12 MeV and is used to identify all the impurities, while the intensity of the prompt /spl gamma/-rays results in the abundances of the isotopes.

articleTitle: Measurement of electro-refraction in GaAs/AlGaAs multiple quantum well waveguide structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Presents a direct approach to precisely measure changes in refractive index (/spl Delta/n) of GaAs/AlGaAs Multiple Quantum Well (MQW) wave guide structures as a function of applied electric field across the MQW layers. The results of /spl Delta/n(E) are useful for developing electro-optic quantum well devices.

articleTitle: A novel torsion balance for the measurement of the Newtonian gravitational constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.A torsion balance has been built for the measurement of the Newtonian gravitational constant that takes advantage of the particular properties of a wide thin torsion strip under heavy load. The test mass is in the form of an assembly of four 0.47 kg masses suspended from a Cu-Se torsion strip 1.25 mm wide and 30 micrometers thick and 80 mm long. The source mass is an assembly of four 10 kg masses that can be turned to different positions with respect to the test masses. Preliminary tests of the system show that the relatively large gravitational signal produces a gravitational signal that, in air at atmospheric pressure, should easily be measurable to 0.1%. As we expect from our previous experience with torsion strips, an excellent zero stability is observed. A measurement of G with an uncertainty of 1% will be made soon to test all the systems and it is hoped to reach an uncertainty of 0.1% within a reasonably short time.

articleTitle: Measurement laser complex for reproduction and transfer of the size of the length unit in the great lengths area
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.Measurement laser complex comprises: (a) a reference measurement laser system of Razmer type; (b) a long-range laser phase motion meter of IPL-FD type. The size of the length unit reproduced by measurement laser system of Razmer type certificated by the working standard of the length unit VETU-1-1-93 is transferred to the long-range (about 5000 m) motion meter of IPL-FD type by comparison of them on the linear interference comparator ILK-25. The long-range laser motion meter IPL-FD is based on a wave length measure, which is realized by means of a stabilized laser radiation generator working in the regime of generation of two longitudinal modes. It is experimentally stated that instrumental error of this range-finder does not exceed 0.17 mm and when the correspondent measurement technique is applied the error can be reduced to 0.05 mm.

articleTitle: Measurement of proton gyromagnetic ratio in low field method [of atom magnetic resonance]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An uniform field space with precision better than 0.1 ppm for 2 cm radius volume, is obtained using a main and four auxiliary current sources. The main 1 A current has been stabilized to 0.1 ppm by using the Cs atoms magnetic resonance technique.

articleTitle: Comparison of rf power meters using two air-line impedance standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A method to calibrate a coaxial RF power meter by comparison with a standard power meter is described, where the ratio of the mismatch factors is determined using two calculable coaxial air-line impedance standards. First experimental results of measurements performed in the coaxial 7 mm/N technique at frequencies from 2 GHz to 18 GHz are presented.

articleTitle: Preliminary absolute frequency measurement of a diode laser locked to a two-photon hyperfine transition of rubidium at 385 THz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have performed a first preliminary measurement of the absolute frequency (v=385.285 THz, /spl lambda/=778.1 nm) of a diode laser frequency-stabilized to the (F/sub 8/=3, F/sub e/=5) hyperfine component of the 58/sub 1/2 /-5D/sub 5/2/ two-photon absorption of /sup 85/Rb, using a frequency chain which synthesizes the 13th harmonic of our laboratory CO/sub 2//OsO/sub 4/ frequency standard at 29 THz.

articleTitle: Long term stabilization of a CO/sub 2/ laser on an OsO/sub 4/ molecular beam
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows.A high spectral purity CO/sub 2/ laser has been stabilized on an OsO/sub 4/ transition observed in molecular beam for the realization of an accurate frequency standard.

articleTitle: Establishment of the volt at CENAM of Mexico
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A voltage standard system based on a Josephson junction series array to represent the volt at Centro Nacional de Metrologia (CENAM) has been established. This paper describes early efforts to set the system up. Tests upon the Josephson array were carried out and preliminary results of the system's performance are presented.

articleTitle: Precise null balancing technique for 10-V Josephson junction array voltage standard system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Precise null balancing technique has developed for 10-V Josephson junction array voltage standard system (10-V JJAVS). New technique is achieved by (1) precise capturing of the desired Josephson step, (2) millimeter-wave adjustment for making strict null balancing, (3) use of a stable chopper-type digital voltmeter (DVM) as a null detector.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of a microcalorimeter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A waveguide microcalorimeter in the frequency range of 18 GHz-26.5 GHz is described. The systematic uncertainties due to microcalorimeter correction factor are discussed. Microcalorimeter using a curve fitting method can reduce the measurement time of the effective efficiencies measurement by a factor of 2. The results of measurements are presented and compared with the data from NIST.

articleTitle: A test standard for calibrating high accurate ADC and DAC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In this paper, a test standard system for measuring ADC and DAC is introduced. By a computer, ADC and DAC can be measured automatically with 24 bits resolution and 1 ppm linearity. The testing speed can be up to 10 KHz.

articleTitle: L-CsPhR sensors in the system of measurement and control of optical transparent environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A sensor that includes a laser and coordinato-sensitive photoreceiver (CsPhR) intended for the thickness-quantity precise measurement of the optical transparent environment such as the glass tubes in fluorescent lighting production, is described. An automatic system based on sliding mode control t technique is described which maintains an invariable thickness of the tube-sides, changing the velocity of tube stretching from a stove(kiln). The angle of incidence and the angle of light rays going-out of the flat parallel plate are equal to each other.

articleTitle: Dimensional measurements of a silicon sphere
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: For a precision determination of Avogadro's constant, N/sub A/, the volume of a nearly perfect silicon sphere of 1 kg and about 90 mm diameter, made of a single-crystal, is to be measured with a relative uncertainty of 10/sup -7/. For this, a new interferometric method is used to measure the diameter and its variations in large number of orientations with uncertainties in the sub-nm range.

articleTitle: Influence of infrared illumination on precision measurements of the integer quantum Hall effect
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The preliminary result reported here unambiguously shows that infrared illumination of a nonfully quantized QHE sample can restore its ideal behaviour. Differences as large as 0.1 ppm in the Hall resistance have disappeared when the sample is illuminated by 150 ms pulses of infrared light. In parallel, the contact resistances of nonideal terminals have been found to decrease with the illumination time, although some high resistance contacts did not show any dependence on illumination. In addition, the illumination leads to an increase of the critical current, although the way this increase is taking place seems to be nonuniversal.

articleTitle: Experimental study of quantum current standard at ETL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In the course of studying the quantum current standard using the single electron tunneling at ETL, a small junction array, a microwave filter and a dilution refrigerator have been developed as key equipments to set up a total experimental apparatus. Testing results of those key equipments are reported.

articleTitle: A buoyancy-free mass comparator with sub-ppm precision for use in a superconducting magnetic levitation system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A system for measuring mass without making correction for the buoyancy of air with a standard uncertainty better than 1 ppm has been developed. The system was originally developed for measuring the mass of the floating body of the superconducting magnetic levitation system.

articleTitle: Amplitude noise and linewidth reduction of an Ar/sup +/ laser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: FM spectroscopy is used for frequency stabilizing an Ar/sup +/ laser at 515 nm with respect to a passive cavity. Preliminary reduction of amplitude fluctuations is performed. The laser's frequency will then be referenced to that of an hyperfine component of iodine, in order to realize an optical frequency standard.

articleTitle: Diode lasers with external optical feedback for small displacement measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new approach to non-contact investigation of small displacements by measuring a diode laser frequency shift was demonstrated. The laser frequency shift is due to an optical feedback from a surface of the moving object and proportional to the object displacement. The technique was applied for calibration of standard accelerometer.

articleTitle: Capacitance scaling system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A capacitance scaling system has been developed and consists of a commercially available four-terminal-pair LCR meter, an inductive voltage divider, and a 1000 pF air dielectric capacitor. It can calibrate capacitors up to 1 /spl mu/F in the frequency range from 50 Hz to 100 kHz. The combined standard uncertainty for 0.01 /spl mu/F at 100 kHz is estimated to be /spl plusmn/73 fF (7.3 parts in 10/sup 6/).

articleTitle: Double circuit quadrature bridge for comparison of quantum Hall resistors with capacitors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A quadrature bridge for comparison of two 12,906.4035 Ohm quantized Hall resistors (or two resistance standards) and two 10000 pF capacitors is described. The bridge has two identical current circuits and allows one to connect directly the potential leads of the four-terminal impedances to be compared.

articleTitle: Noise and balance point characteristics of a.c. and d.c. bridges used for a.c/d.c. and d.c. resistance standards comparisons
publicationTitle: Proceedings of 20th Biennial Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Measurements were performed on a.c. and d.c. resistance standards, using both a.c. and d.c. bridges. The measurements identified the a.c./d.c. difference for both types of resistors. The signal-to-noise present on the combinations of measurements was recorded and their type A uncertainty was evaluated.
